text:
東醫寶鑑內景篇卷之二

御醫忠勤貞亮扈
聖功臣崇禄大夫陽平君臣許浚奉
教撰

血為榮

榮者水穀之精氣也。和調於五藏。灑陳於六府。乃能入於脈也。化以為血。以榮四末。內注五藏六府。以應刻數焉。其血乃成於中焦。受氣於水穀。乃化而為赤。是謂道乃又乃能入於脈。載之精也。故

行氣而內綜絡脈六上府下掌血而能視得足而能握。臥則血歸於肝。肝受血而能視。足受血而能步。掌受血而能握。指得血而能攝。目得血而能視。

厚薄宣布於肝。日宣精於之。生灌。能血而而能視得而足能握。

陰之長取汁變化而赤為血常也。以故食血盛則形盛。血弱則形衰。陽注而能陽血生。

朝鮮總督府圖書之印
translation:
Dongui Bogam (Treasured Mirror of Eastern Medicine), Inner Landscape Section, Volume 2

Royal Physician, Loyal, Diligent, and Upright, Escort of the Sacred Merit Subject, Senior First Rank, Lord of Yangpyeong, Your Servant Heo Jun, by Royal Command, Compiled.

Blood as Nourishment (Rong)

Nourishment (Rong) is the essential qi of water and grain. It harmonizes within the five viscera and spreads throughout the six bowels, and thus can enter the vessels. It is transformed into blood to nourish the four extremities, and internally flows into the five viscera and six bowels, corresponding to the measured intervals. This blood is formed in the middle burner, receiving qi from water and grain, and is transformed to become red — this is what is called the pathway. It then enters the vessels, carrying the essence.

Qi moves and internally connects the network vessels; the upper part governs blood so that the eyes can see and the feet can grasp. When one lies down, blood returns to the liver. When the liver receives blood, it can see. When the feet receive blood, they can walk. When the palms receive blood, they can grasp. When the fingers receive blood, they can hold. When the eyes receive blood, they can see.

The liver spreads and distributes [blood], day by day sending out essence, nourishing and irrigating [the body], so that blood enables sight, the feet enable movement, and the hands enable grasping.

When yin grows, it draws out fluid and transforms it, turning red to become blood — this is the constant principle. Therefore, when one eats food and blood is abundant, the body is robust; when blood is weak, the body declines. Yang infuses [the body] and thus blood is generated.

脈法

失血脈皆見日脈得諸脈貴沈細浮乃爲難治。脈正訣曰諸證據一身可之

熟失血時乃吐脈至而失血止。又曰靈樞日吐血之不脈必止。大血正訣曰諸證據

大經日大脈時日吐脈至者難血鉗病酩者死。又吐又脈日腹膨細脈便反脈

丹浮漢大而吐者至血者。博。難解鉗病若者死。而吐語實血者難治。小弱

血者盞生脈實大大者數死者。連諸失數者景日難治。而吐語實血者難治小弱

translation:
Blood is paired with Qi

When [qi] is weak and declining, the physical form [suffers].

Qi stops circulation, blood stops; when qi is warm, it covers like water; qi is the commander of blood, like wind directing wood — when qi moves, blood moves above, where qi goes blood follows.

Governing [the body] means guiding circulation; reaching the upper [regions], regulating what is there; qi and breath then cause the blood's area to flow smoothly; in illness and cold, blood and dampness regulate qi — within one breath it can be assessed throughout the whole body.

Pulse Methods

In blood loss, all pulse [presentations] seen daily — the pulse obtaining various [qualities], the prized [pulse] being sunken, thin, floating — [these] are difficult to treat. The Pulse Essentials says: in all such patterns, throughout the body, one may assess [them].

When heat [causes] blood loss, if at the time of vomiting the pulse arrives and the blood loss stops — again, the Lingshu says: in vomiting blood, the pulse must stop. In great blood loss, the Essentials says: in all such patterns...

In major channels: when the pulse is large and one is vomiting, [if] the pulse arrives at that point, it is difficult [to treat]; in severe illness the patient dies. Again, vomiting with an abdominal distension, thin pulse, loose bowels, and contradictory pulse [signs].

[When] floating [pulse], as in the Han [formula], with large [pulse] and vomiting arriving with blood — [this is] hard to resolve; in severe illness, if the patient dies; with vomiting and replete, full blood, [the condition] is difficult to treat; [pulse that is] small and weak...

Blood [conditions with] full, replete, large pulse — those [patients] die; among various [cases], with rapid pulse it is difficult to treat; with vomiting and replete blood it is difficult to treat; small and weak [pulse]...

Heat Can Injure Blood

Heat can injure blood; the heart [rules] the nine [openings]; heat and blazing cannot be remedied; the heart stir-fries [i.e., overheats]; when heat is extreme, heat injures blood; blood exits from the heart, [the patient] feels faint and wishes to cleanse [the body].

七情動血

謂知陰又不可無也。緯。是丹溪曰諸血見熱則行見血皆熱證。陽陰虛降則升血無歸經血。又曰陽盛陰虛則降有餘不足補諸鮮補陽盛。故傷者赤色得寒則凝澀者故鮮溢上者赤得血色也。黑色也淡者從血日黑色軟則發出上鼻法血富皆補。一言而蔽之。又不可一言而蔽。

則知其要者一言而蔽之。又不可無也。隨氣則越越出口上鼻發出法血富皆補陽盛。是也又日諸血見熱則行見血皆熱證。

動血。溢嘔血。則但怒氣逆從血上者使人暴暴甚廉心又又日日怒大則怒形則氣迺甚氣。

血溢鼻血。而怒氣逆諸鏡從血上喝使人暴暴甚廉心內又又日日怒則怒師相以請甚氣。抑師則氣迺甚氣全則。

行陰宜老用是保命生地玄黃土散火內臟傷血七上情緒傷者懷安全則。

過思動傷心脾失能生血暴散能動肝又血積五血七愛情動傷者暴安。

喜熱傷肝解而脾失控腎皆連命散能動肝又日藏五志愛動傷者暴。

此血肝則怒自愈兩嘔血遇暴以者傷肝黃保連命散貼青黛五胡大甘草平嚴失。

其肝無兩受暴心則氣遞彼柴而甘草。

淋血無故肝從大又起勞過錯經而以致行陰大而肝不納血故。
translation:
Seven Emotions Stirring Blood

It is said that one must understand yin, yet one cannot do without it. This is what Danxi (Zhu Danxi, the Yuan dynasty physician) said: "All blood disorders arise from heat; when blood is seen, it is always a heat pattern." When yang is excess and yin is deficient, the blood fails to return to the channels. He also said: when yang is exuberant and yin is deficient, there is excess above and deficiency below — supplementing the yang excess. Hence, fresh bright-red blood that is warm flows freely; blood that encounters cold congeals and becomes sluggish; pale blood comes from the channels; dark black blood is softened and issues upward from the nose and mouth — the method of enriching blood fully supplements yang exuberance. In one phrase it may be summed up. Yet it cannot be summed up in one phrase alone.

To know the essentials, one phrase suffices to encompass all. Yet one cannot do without it. When the qi rebels upward, blood overflows out of the mouth and nose — the method of enriching blood supplements yang exuberance.

When blood stirs, it overflows and causes vomiting of blood. When anger causes qi to rebel upward, blood rushes upward, making people violently agitated in the heart. Anger then causes the qi to be extreme.

When blood overflows through the nose, anger causes qi rebellion; blood rushes upward, causing violent agitation of the heart. Suppressing the teacher/guide, the qi becomes extreme.

For disorders of yin, it is appropriate to use the Baoming Shengdi Xuanhuang Tu Powder (Life-Preserving Rehmannia-Coptis-Earth Formula) for fire damaging the blood internally — the seven emotions injure and cause agitation.

Excessive thought and worry injures the heart and spleen, impairing the generation of blood; sudden dispersion stirs the liver.

Joy and heat injure the liver; the spleen loses control; the kidneys and all are linked — suddenly the liver is stirred.

This blood of the liver — anger causes spontaneous recovery; vomiting of blood suddenly; injury to the liver; the formula Lian Ming San with Qingdai (indigo), Wuhu (five tiger ingredients), Dagan Cao (licorice) — calming and soothing.

Its liver is without fault — both sides suffer sudden violence; the heart then causes qi to shift, moving with licorice.

Blood in the urine without cause comes from the liver; from great exertion and overwork, the channels become disrupted, leading to disorder of yin; thus the liver fails to contain the blood.

translation:
Internal Injury and Blood Loss

Various Syndromes of Blood Loss

When there is overflow and excess, suddenly and acutely, overeating and drinking causes the vessels to become full; irregular daily activities and overexertion externally —

When there is surplus, blood exits from the seven yang collaterals, injuring the blood vessels; yang collaterals injured cause blood to overflow internally; afterward the vessels fill with blood and overflow externally.

When blood seeps and percolates through, it enters the intestines; taxation causes blood loss; various syndromes arise below, with blood moving downward through the bowels and urine, accumulating in the large and small intestines, causing vomiting; the bladder causes bloody stool; blood overflows internally, leading to blood deficiency.

Phlegm and stasis, dark yellow, stagnant and blocked; heat rises, transforming yin; when deficient yang accumulates as redness, great yang causes large and small bowel bleeding in the urine.

Colors: pain, itching, heat on the skin; when yang and yin are extreme, there is decay; deficient yang accumulates, causing vomiting; when the organ is overwhelmed, there is bloody stool; when blood overflows internally, blood deficiency results.

Green-tinted blood originates from the stomach, entering upward; it may arise from the mouth, the nose, or the skin; daily it transforms into dark phlegm; blood rises upward; the person likes to hemorrhage; water diarrhea opens externally; then heat consumes the blood.

Blood issuing from below comes from the lungs, or from the blood itself; vomiting of blood rises upward from the nose; what is called blood-streaked throat.

Blood exits following the lung; it may come from the large intestine; blood coming from the lungs arrives with vomiting; it exits through the throat as blood-streaked phlegm.

Blood exits through sweat pores; blood comes from the muscles; blood comes from the root of the teeth; blood comes from the intestinal wind; in the small intestine, phlegm carries blood; from the root of the tongue, blood is regulated.

Nine types arise from coughing; the tongue has blood in all cases; examining the color of new and old blood; blood is regulated from within; nine types of blood exit; from regulating the blood and pulse, blood exits from the diaphragm; blood exits from regulation.

Distinguishing New and Old Blood by Color

Black color — summer-heat syndrome. Red color — old blood. Red rinse — black color. Also resembling smoke and soot — a smoke-soot syndrome. Clear water color — cold syndrome.

translation:
Accumulated Blood (蓄血)

Symptoms and Signs: In yang-type excess patterns, there is repeated passage of fresh bright blood. In yin-type patterns, as the condition worsens, the stool resembles the color of liver tissue, initially brownish in color.

When there is mania, blood accumulation, forgetfulness, and suppressed fire causing dryness and scorching, the condition resembles sheep's blood stagnation; on that very day the color turns dark, and the stool becomes brownish.

With accumulated blood mixed with yellow and black hues, there is frequent urination; as the disease progresses, blood accumulates, and there is injury to the small intestine; with cold-heat alternation, the disease manifests with dark urine resembling that pattern.

Below: the patient cries out, the illness manifests day and night, the stool is heavy, thirst persists, and blood accumulates; the small intestine is affected; frequent urination with no desire to drink water; in milder cases it resembles mania with dark urine.

Upper and middle: scorching in the upper burner; the affected region shows good signs of blood; mild epidemic-like confusion; small frequent urination with no desire; the condition resembles mania with dark urine.

When feces become dry and hard in the lower abdomen, with hardness and pain, Tao Ren Cheng Qi Tang (Peach Pit Order-Resolving Decoction) is appropriate to prevent blood stagnation in the middle and lower burners.

For dryness and binding, use Sheng Di, Yu Huang, Da Gan Cao, Jian Tao Ren to break up stagnant blood. Tao Ren in all cases breaks up stagnant blood. Ginger and Tribulus are also used.

For blood accumulation in the lower burner, use wood-based and spirit-strengthening herbs including Wu Huang, Da Gan Cao, and Jian Tao Ren to expel the accumulation. For accumulated blood in the lower burner, ginger and Tribulus are used.韭 (chive) juice, Ling Dan, and other herbs combined with Wu Huang, Da Gan Cao, Ling Dan, Fu Tao Ren all break up stagnant blood.

translation:
Saengjiwhang-tang (Fresh Rehmannia Decoction)

Use half a liang of fresh Rehmannia; pound it cold, press out one large sheng of juice. [Indicated for] blood-pattern disorders with black [discoloration], small sunken thin faint pulse, and [conditions affecting] the gallbladder and qi; especially suitable for those who are weak, and also for those who are delirious or agitated.

[Ingredients include:] ten leaves, one piece of stir-fried [ingredient], one sheng, half a sheng of juice, half a sheng — use dried peach kernel, half a sheng ground, two liang stir-fried, ten parts water, ten sheng, stir-fried together with water, lightly dry-fried.

Compare this prescription with the carp soup — test against each other in cold [constitution]. Take in two portions of nine [doses]; first take a small amount, fearing [adverse effects]; when the time comes, allow nine portions; when blood in the stool fails to stop after three sheng of water, stop again and decoct again.

Prognostic Signs in Blood Disorders

When [the condition is] severe and the patient cannot bear heat, [the patient] will die quickly; when the pulse flows smoothly, recovery is easy. When [there is] no tidal fever and the blood discharge is light with heat in the body and tidal [fever], [prognosis is good].

When [the condition involves] vigorous lung [qi] and the pulse is full, it will break up the blood; if the form is like [boiling] heat surging upward with flushed complexion, large [open] mouth and nose, white [pallor] appearing — if this occurs afterward and downward bleeding is treated, recovery is possible; if blood is excessive and the heart and lower [burner] are hot, this is severe.

When the pulse is small and rapid, this indicates [pathology in] the flesh and membranes. If the pulse is small and forceful yet stops moving, and there is blood in the stool with abdominal fullness, pain radiating to the back and abdomen — this is serious.

When downward movement occurs again and the condition transforms into festering and counterflow, with the flesh and membranes separating and the pulse becoming thin — this is a counterflow pulse. [This is among the] critical [signs].

亡血脫血證

見血身熱者易治易脈大者難治難治日者邪勝也又易治為日者血滲上也或行涼脈或靜脈

下血者臨或也其吐治哂者難下也自行若無癥順而其下易治行忽為然仲痢景者云蓄者上行身涼脈靜或

進下也今者當血自愈若上行而無景象其下人忽行為然仲痢云蓄者上行或

去熱不得知吉也者死。仲景曰此血觀之者病惡上血氣名脈者其邪疾證行

translation:
Loss of Blood and Collapse of Blood: Signs and Symptoms

When blood loss is accompanied by fever, the condition is easy to treat. When the pulse is large, it is difficult to treat. When treatment is said to be difficult, it means evil qi is dominant. When it is said to be easy to treat, it means blood is seeping upward, or the pulse is cool or calm.

In cases of bleeding downward: if there is vomiting, treatment below is difficult. If it flows naturally without symptoms, following the normal course, and then descends, treatment is easy. If suddenly the flow changes, this is what Zhongjing calls blood accumulation rising upward, or the body becomes cool and the pulse calm.

When descending: currently, blood will heal on its own. If it moves upward without signs, then suddenly the person's flow changes — this is what Zhongjing refers to as accumulation, rising upward.

Regarding heat — if one cannot determine whether the prognosis is good or bad, the person dies. Zhongjing said: observe this blood — if the disease worsens, if blood and qi are named in the pulse, then evil and disease are manifested.

[Further passages discuss the difficulty of self-treatment, injury from cold, Yang syndrome, blood in the stool, downward bleeding, and damage to the blood pathways.]

Regarding blood congestion already formed, when vomiting stops, one may gently examine — if the disease intensifies over several days, the bladder and heart will be exhausted.

Regarding the Sea of Blood: if the head is not well, color is white, the body is deficient in blood. Furthermore, if the Chong vessel loses its vital essence, the face appears without luster.

Li Dongyuan said: if the pulse is thin and rough, and the body is not at ease, then the body's pulse is full but vacuous and hollow inside. [The formulas follow.]

Formula [No. 39]: [Ingredients listed] — honey pills the size of a large seed of Chinese dodder, take one hundred pills each time with rice wine, decoction of Ophiopogon, etc. Divide into portions; the right side of the chest formula.

translation:
Methods to Stop Nosebleed

For treating nosebleeds that have persisted for a long time and have not responded to various medicines: Take a large sheet of white paper, soak it in cold water, and place it on top of the head — this stops nosebleeds immediately. If still not stopped, roll paper into plugs and insert into both nostrils; the bleeding will stop. If still not stopped, and blood is coming from both nostrils, apply crushed garlic (one clove, peeled and ground into a paste like a cake) to the Yongquan acupoint (Kidney 1): if the left nostril bleeds, apply to the right foot; if the right nostril bleeds, apply to the left foot. Take the formula in water. Formula: equal parts of Sanleng (sparganium) and Maidong (ophiopogon), grind into powder, mix with cold water, apply to the nose for bleeding that will not stop.

Dispersing method for treating severe nosebleeds that will not stop: Take half a sheet of paper, fold into two pieces, twist into ten paper rolls, plug both nostrils — bleeding stops at once. Or plug the middle of both nostrils; oral bleeding stops immediately.

Medicines: Green vitriol (green alum) — apply to stop nosebleed from the right nostril; blood stops.

Vomiting Blood and Spitting Blood

Soup (decoction) stimulating the lungs, with Sophora flower, connecting the stomach internally — for cases where vomiting blood occurs with hiccup sounds, use Qianjin (Thousand Gold) Banxia Dihuang Tang (Decoction); for deficiency cases with small irregularities.

For nosebleed where blood has seeped from the pores: the blood is suspected to come from between the heart and lungs, flowing into the stomach and then vomited. It may appear in amounts like beans, or as much as ginger-sized pieces. After drinking alcohol, at the time of vomiting, blood comes out from the lungs after vomiting, sometimes in amounts of one he (合) or more, sometimes mixed with spirits.

translation:
This passage is from the internal medicine section discussing conditions related to vomiting blood (hematemesis) and gastrointestinal disorders:

When one eats excessively or is overwhelmed by cold qi and the stomach cannot digest properly, one suffers from irritability, nausea, vomiting, thirst, and vomiting of blood. For stomach injury causing vomiting of blood with red blood in the vessels, add Sichuan Xiong (Ligusticum), Zijin (purple herb), dried ginger, and kudzu. For difficulty with stomach and vomiting of blood from the mouth, red blood in the abdomen, it is appropriate to regulate internally and add Huangqi (astragalus), Buzhong pills, Renshen (ginseng), Lianzi (lotus seed) decoction. For vomiting of blood with lung deficiency, use Sanhuang (three yellow herbs) decoction with scutellaria and dried ginger.

For chest symptoms with vomiting, add Rehmannia; for deficiency, use kudzu and Huangqi pills with Chahong decoction internally to nourish the throat and stop vomiting of blood. When blood becomes solidified in the decoction from vomiting blood, exceeding this degree indicates over-heating, apply Menjian (door decoction) to regulate.

For patterns of vomiting blood from the middle burner, taking the Four Materials Decoction with cold properties, for black blood formations, use Renshen (ginseng) Decoction; for immediate vomiting of blood, add Xiong and dry ginger to guide downward.

For fire-induced vomiting of blood in midday, when one perceives it is good to regulate, use the Four Materials Decoction with Taohe (peach kernel) and Huanglian Jiedu (Coptis detoxifying) Decoction; if overheated apply Menjian decoction to regulate downward.

For treating stagnant blood and fire injury, when cold causes blood loss and sweating stops, enter into the heart to transform phlegm; if heat arises, apply Shanghuo (mountain fire) disease compresses and heated decoctions. For difficult defecation with lumps, adjust accordingly.

For general treatment of excessive bleeding, use kudzu and Yang-lightening formulas, Dijuang (Rehmannia) cooked, add Shenhual (spirit transformation), Ziye (gardenia), Maogen (imperata root), and meditate on the abdomen.

For regulation and weight management, use Taoziren (peach kernel), Lianzi (lotus seed), heart qi decoction, Yueju Wan, Heishen Powder, Baizhu (atractylodes) formulas, Tianmendong (asparagus root), with therapeutic applications for the stomach.

For the seven raw herb formulas, use Sisheng (four raw) Drink, Qingrejiedu (heat-clearing detoxifying) Decoction, Huaye (flower leaf), and Shisan Powder, Wushen Decoction, with Ouju (lotus root) juice for nosebleed and vomiting of blood.

This page from Dongui Bogam describes treatments for coughing up blood (hemoptysis) and related respiratory conditions involving phlegm and fire pathology. The text covers several formulas and clinical discussions:

On coughing blood (咯血): When there is fresh red blood coughed up, this is due to deficiency of yin and flaring of fire. Use decoctions with kudzu (葛), bamboo (竹), and formulas that enrich yin and descend fire.

When blood comes up mixed with phlegm, this arises from heat in the mountains (i.e., accumulation of heat). It is difficult to treat. Use formulas that clear heat, descend the fire, and stop bleeding. Moutan (牡丹) and Four Substances Decoction (四物湯) with additions are recommended. Tianhua fen (天花粉), Chenpi (橘皮) and other herbs are used depending on whether phlegm or blood predominates.

Dragon Brain Difficult Perilla Pill (龍腦難蘇九): This formula uses Xuanshuang (玄霜), Xueli (雪梨) decoction, Ejiao (阿膠), loquat (枇杷), and related herbs. It treats coughing of blood with phlegm accumulation and heat.

For the pill preparation: Take equal parts of the herbs, grind to powder, extract the juice, mix with honey, combine with bupleurum (柴胡), processed over slow fire, form into pills the size of firmiana seeds, take ten pills each time, then pound into a paste with ginseng (人參) four liang, and huang (黃) [huang qi or huangqin].

The previous six medicines are ground together, kneaded and formed into pills, or made as large as soybean size, decocted and taken, ten pills each time.

Xuan Shuang Xue Li Gao (Frost-Snow Pear Paste)

One dose, decocted in water. Treats coughing of blood, relieves taxation of the heart. Take the juice of six snow pears (removing the core), two jin of juice, for chronic cough from overexertion. Urinary Blood

The Inner Classic states: when heat from the middle burner shifts downward and the bladder is heated, urine with blood results, forming strangury and urinary blood.

The small intestine is not the same as strangury; blood exits because heat accumulates, shifts, and causes pain. If small intestinal heat moves and causes urinary blood, the pain shifts and becomes difficult.

Treatment: use Poria and ophiopogon decoction to nourish yin and clear the intestines.

translation:
Blood in Stool

The Inner Canon (Neijing) states: When the yin is bound (jie yin), there is one sheng of blood in the stool; when bound twice, two sheng; when bound three times, three sheng. The commentary explains: when evil qi lodges in the blood vessels and cannot circulate, binding occurs. Because the blood is bound, it cannot move freely. When bound twice, two sheng; when bound three times, three sheng.

Dongyuan (Li Dongyuan) said: Because the evil cannot move, the blood becomes bound, and the channels and collaterals fall out of harmony. When both vessels are bound, blood cannot circulate and stagnates. For blood appearing after stool, use the Small Bean and Angelica Powder (Xiaodou Danggui San) and Rehmannia-Angelica Powder.

When disease is in the intestines and viscera, if it descends to the intestinal region, use Pingwei Diyu Tang (Stomach-Calming Sanguisorba Decoction) for blood accumulation. When the yin and yang vessels bind and blood cannot circulate, there is blockage.

For cases of dark intestinal blood: when the pulse of the yin channels is not harmonized and yin is obstructed, use Yingeldan as the primary formula. For blood appearing before stool, Zhang Zhongjing observed that this type involves blood accumulating first. For blood appearing after stool, it is because the blood has stagnated; the viscera fails to move it, so it remains.

The primary decoction is Lianzi Tang (Coptis Decoction). For reduced original qi with downward blockage, use the dispersing formula; add Buzhong Yiqi Tang (Middle-Tonifying Qi-Boosting Decoction), Chengyu Ju, and Red Bean Angelica Rehmannia Powder.

For cases of internal injury from alcohol toxin and improper diet, use Pingwei San (Stomach-Calming Powder) with added ingredients, decoct with Buzhong Yiqi Tang, combined with Red Bean Angelica Rehmannia Powder.

Pingwei Diyu Tang (Stomach-Calming Sanguisorba Decoction)

Ingredients each in 5 fen: dried ginger, Angelica root, wheat-processed preparation, dry-fried ginger root, white peony root, two portions of Aucklandia root, tangerine peel, decocted with kernel, pound root, licorice.

White atractylodes, magnolia bark, tangerine peel, each one qian.

Jieyin Dan (Yin-Unbinding Elixir)

Each 5 zhu: moxa-treated Polygonum multiflorum, Saposhnikovia root, bitter orange shell, each 5 qian; Clematis root, astragalus, tangerine peel, decocted with kernel, licorice.

Skin formula: dried ginger, for blood in stool, Angelica, portion made with medicated leaven, kudzu root, white magnolia bark, hemp, aconite (blast-processed), red tea, one qian.

translation:
Intestinal Dysentery (Changbyeok)
Tooth Bleeding (Chi-nuk)

Symptoms

Three [ingredients]: acorns, five seeds, ten large, nine cooked alum water, taken orally.

Enter through the tooth gate; detailed discussion follows. Tooth bleeding — blood seeping from the tooth crevices is called "chi-nuk" (tooth bleeding). It is also called "ya-seon" (tooth proclamation), belonging to the Stomach channel. Blood oozing from the tooth crevices.

When blood flows from the Yangming channel into the gums and enters the Shaoyin channel, these two channels intersect; this is also called tooth blood emerging from the tooth crevices.

Blood coming up to the head — most cases are due to not being aware externally; use Green Robe Powder applied locally, and internally take water to vigorously rinse the mouth, then the gums will close and the bleeding will stop.

During the day, most people use raw rehmannia or gold-connecting powder, small thistle decoction, to detoxify; rinse the mouth vigorously and the gums will close and stop bleeding.

For the tooth angle, use the prior decoction or powder with raw rehmannia and small thistle powder; see water to detoxify; rinse vigorously and the gums will close and stop bleeding.

Green Robe Powder (Nokpo-san):
Treats tooth bleeding; grind to powder; if bleeding does not stop, use bamboo shavings or stir-fried pagoda tree flowers, and a small amount of appropriate herbs.

Jing-fei Powder (Hyeong-bi-san):
Treats tooth bleeding; use appropriate amount of tea, yellow flowers, pagoda tree flowers stir-fried, and a small amount of appropriate herbs.

Oriole Gold Powder (Aengeum-san):
Regularly treats tooth bleeding; use bamboo shavings, bitter herbs, salt, and cyperus root; immediately stops bleeding; rinse and hold in mouth.

Small Thistle Powder (Soji-san):
Stir-fry and treat; five appropriate measures; for tooth bleeding, grind the right ingredients to powder with sooty bamboo, small thistle, salt, and cyperus root; immediately stops; rinse and hold in mouth.

Another formula:
Green bamboo scraping soaked in blood, add a small amount, soak overnight; also use concentrated bamboo leaf liquid with salt applied and held in the mouth.

Diseases of the Heavenly (Head/Mouth) Region — Various Symptoms

[Section on mouth and tooth ailments:]
Decoct bitter herbs into a strong tea; use ginseng decoction — for toothache, oral bleeding from the gums and teeth.

Take coptis (Huanglian), open the pores; use cortex lycii (wolfberry root bark) decoction; after applying, brush the tongue. For tongue sores, roast and grind to powder and apply. Another recipe using small red beans.

Tongue Sore [Shé Chóng] Formula: Take soybeans, roast to ash; take one portion of ox [bile or similar], pound and crush, add vinegar and water, two parts, combine the juice and take orally. Also, pick tongue flower [herb], roast and grind the maggots to powder and apply. Another small red bean recipe.

Mosquito Larva Powder (Wén Jū Sǎn): Treats bleeding from the surface of the tongue. Take the above ingredients to the amount of blood, mix with spring water, take five portions of tangerine [preparation], benefit the white [coating]. For spontaneous sweating, this is also appropriate. [Acupuncture point] Hegu (LI-4), three intervals.

Blood Sweating: When the meridians receive [pathogenic heat], in cases of extreme heat, blood comes out mixed with sweat — this is a remarkable condition. The garment becomes stained. This is called "mosquito larva blood" [i.e., blood sweating]. The command herb is appropriate; sweating should also use Astragalus (Huangqi) daily.

[For] redness, use Four-Ingredient Decoction. When caused by great illness or injury with sweating, use coptis, printed on the garment — qi disperses like mosquito-larva blood. Follow the ancestral prescription named "Daily Command." Also for three intervals [acupuncture].

Slow [pulse] at Limen point; in winter, moisten the blood, regulate and take. Also use cinnabar; for postpartum blood sweating, use gold and silver vessels [to boil medicine].

translation:
Methods and Medicines for Treating Blood Disorders

When using medicinal formulas for blood, one should not use a single drug alone to move blood, nor should one use only cold medicines to stop bleeding. Those who have taken medicines for a long time without effect have generally used the formulas improperly (often overusing warm preparations). According to the principle of principal, ministerial, assistant, and guiding herbs, prolonged treatment that fails to stop bleeding is problematic. For cases of profuse bleeding that will not stop, wine-prepared Angelica root (酒歸) is used.

Wine-fried medicines of this type must be combined with acrid and warming herbs to raise and guide the action of Ligusticum (川芎). For longstanding cases of persistent bleeding with blood stasis and numbness, Ligusticum (川芎) is again appropriate.

When blood is seen moving with heat, there is suspicion of cold obstruction. For stopping bleeding and resolving stasis, formulas incorporating Rehmannia (地黃) and Sophora (側柏) are appropriate, along with Donkey-hide gelatin (阿膠) for intestinal bleeding. Tao's formula uses fresh Rehmannia, Safflower (紅花), Sappan wood (蘇木), Hundred Herb Frost (百草霜), and Trachycarpus (棕).

For conditions with deficiency and cold, preparations with milk-based gelatin and Cattail pollen (蒲黃), with Ophiopogon (門冬) and Donkey-hide gelatin (阿膠), are appropriate. Tao's formula for clearing and stopping bleeding uses fresh Rehmannia, Safflower, Sappan wood, Hundred Herb Frost, and Trachycarpus charcoal.

For pain syndromes with blood deficiency and cold, use gelatin preparations with Coptis (黃連) and Rehmannia. Each ingredient benefits the blood without causing dryness-heat; dry Ginger (乾薑) and charred Trachycarpus are appropriate here.

To move blood downward effectively, medicines that warm and disperse — such as Siler root (防風) — guide the formula. Upper bleeding is treated by generating blood with Coptis and Rehmannia. Each substance benefits the blood without producing dryness-heat; dry Ginger and charred Trachycarpus are suitable.

When blood cannot carry qi back into proper circulation, the blood color is fresh red; fresh Rehmannia is used, and if the pulse is surging and excess, Licorice (甘草) is needed to supplement the blood. The combined decoction for men and women addresses internal heat with blood stasis, using dry Ginger and charred Trachycarpus.

For blood diarrhea that will not stop, Angelica root (當歸) is used to harmonize the blood — an excellent method. For blood insufficiency, three qian (approximately 11g) per dose is decocted. The combined men-and-women decoction addresses internal heat and dryness of the blood, using dry Ginger and charred Trachycarpus.

Four Substances Decoction (Siwul-tang / Si Wu Tang):
Ingredients include Ligusticum chuanxiong (Chuan Xiong), which enters the channels; in summer add Scutellaria (Huang Qin); in autumn add Asparagus root (Tian Men Dong) and fresh Rehmannia (Sheng Di Huang); in winter add Cinnamon twig (Gui Zhi). This formula enriches and supplements blood.

translation:
Cedrela Decoction (側柏湯): Take it dissolved in water or in vinegar water, decocted in water with tea; it treats all manner of bleeding conditions including blood in the stool, loss of blood. Also called Bai Tang, also called Ye Bai.

Used together with tea. [Same indications as above.]

Boy's Urine (童子尿): For all cases of deficiency with vomiting blood, coughing blood — in all blood-treating decoctions and medicines, adding one cup of boy's urine greatly enhances the effect. All the sages have said this. It descends fire in all cases and stops it — this is what the sages say.

Take it warm, have the patient drink the boy's urine — one cup per day, in two or three doses. The urine taken fresh is best.

Simple Remedies, Second Section, Nine Types, Two:

Pot Black (百草霜): The soot from the bottom of a village cooking pot. Take the fine powder and use it. When blood sees black it stops. Blow it into the orifice, or use it as a black preparation.

Well-Spring Water (井華水): Taken as a dispersing powder, or taken cold and mixed for swallowing, or used for dryness, or administered as a treatment — it is connected to the apertures and the face, and addresses bleeding; the patient should be informed of this first.

translation:
Fresh Rehmannia (Sheng Di Huang): Treats vomiting of blood. Mix with peppermint juice, or take fresh juice of the cut herb and drink half a cup daily.

Plantain herb and root (Che Qian Cao): Stops bleeding; use cut and dry-fried. Mix the expressed juice with water and take five ge (合). Or take fresh juice of the herb for blood.

Cattail pollen (Pu Huang): Stops bleeding and regulates blood. Decoct and take. Can also be taken raw to supplement blood and astringent bleeding.

Ligusticum (Xiong Qiong): Moves blood when there is blood loss. Decoct and take, or take as powder with raw preparation; three portions. Excellent for cutting through stagnation.

Angelica root (Dang Gui): Treats vomiting; guides blood back, moves blood in all cases, nourishes blood. One dose.

Calamus root (Chang Pu root): Pound and treat; make into powder, take two qian each time for uterine bleeding; decoct in water, cut and take to treat blood disorders.

White taro root (Bai Yu Gen): Can stop vomiting and urinary difficulty. Decoct; for blood conditions, cut and take; for loss of urine, use function preparation.

Mugwort leaf (Ai Ye): Pound and treat; take the expressed juice. For dry conditions, cut and take to astringe. For loss and urinary problems, use the preparation.

Garden burnet (Di Yu): Stops bleeding from bowels and vomiting; for partial blood stasis, astringes. Cut and take.

Greater and lesser thistle (Da Xiao Ji): Take the expressed juice and drink one small cup at a time. Can mix with a little honey and drink. Or pound fresh for use.

translation:
Shepherd's Purse (Qi Jin / 薺金)

[For stopping bleeding, dispersing blood stasis, and treating malignant blood conditions:] Grind into powder, mix with non-juice (chive juice) and children's urine, take with good wine. It disperses congealed blood and malignant blood. Grind into powder, mix with children's urine and good wine together.

Bletilla (Bai Ji / 白芨)
Treats hematemesis (vomiting blood). Also effective for those who have swallowed something that scratched the throat, causing bleeding from the throat and nasal discharge. Regulates and stops tooth bleeding, tongue bleeding, and bleeding going downward. Grind into powder, dry-fry, take with warm wine. The powder truly tonifies the lungs — wonderfully effective. Stops [bleeding].

Pagoda Tree Flower (Huai Hua / 槐花)
One coin-weight in decoction. Regulates blood and stops bleeding. Also stops tooth bleeding and tongue bleeding. Grind into powder, dry-fry until done, take with warm wine.

Chinese Arborvitae Leaf (Ce Bai Ye / 側栢葉)
Treats vomiting of blood and all types of hemorrhage. Decoct with fresh rehmannia juice, take the decoction. Also effective. [It] nourishes Yin.

Pine Soot Ink (Song Yan Mo / 松烟墨)
Grind thickly; or decoct with fresh rehmannia, take the juice to stop bleeding and nourish Yin.

Fresh Thistle Juice (Sheng Ji Zhi / 生薊汁)
Disperses abscesses and stops bleeding. For all cases of bleeding from alcohol, take by drinking. After drinking four cups, one will necessarily feel agitated and uneasy in the chest, but will recover on one's own afterward. Take the juice with the stalk.

Chive Juice (Jiu Zhi / 非汁)
Drink three to four cups; one will necessarily feel agitated and uneasy, but will recover on one's own afterward. Take the juice with the stalk.

translation:
Ash of Tangled Hair (Luan Fa Hui)
Stops all kinds of blood loss — vomiting blood, nosebleed, blood in stool and urine, bleeding from all nine orifices — all are treated by this. Take it dissolved in vinegar water or rice-water and drink it; it may also be taken plain.

Replenishing the Body's Blood: When the body's blood is deficient and the complexion is pale and wan, drink six liang of the blood of a living black dog; taking it repeatedly produces miraculous effects.

Hives (Urticaria): Take the juice, add a small amount of salt, and take it to stop bleeding; by cockcrow the bleeding will cease.

Radish Juice (Luo Bo Zhi): Treats vomiting of blood and nosebleed. Mix with good wine and drink; the condition will stop rapidly and the bleeding will cease. Take eight fen of the juice.

Acupuncture and Moxibustion Methods: It is appropriate to moxa the upper and lower points — Yinbai, Daling, Neiting — three times; the bleeding will be cured immediately. [Points include] Qi Hai, Zhongwan, Shangwan, Zusanli, Zhaohai, Shenmen, and Navel area.

Fei Shu (Lung Back-shu point): Apply moxa according to the patient's age in cones. For taxation-cough with vomiting of blood, and also for nosebleed: moxa Ge Shu (Diaphragm Shu) with a hundred cones.

Moxa seven cones and the bleeding will also stop.

Dongui Bogam states: On vomiting blood, volume two.

text:
魂魄為夢

夢。凡夢皆緣。現魄役真人。又其日形接而為事。神者遇而為夢。則神現存故也。邪氣客於心。則夢邪氣虛實。使飛揚越紛。心虛則夢安其繃衰者。合血少者。目眇少也。血氣少。夢氣少行而精神孤。

別離散。離魂散。使治陽魂風為病。云男別離見。女女見男。宜附此去邪。柱蒲乾各薑根三苗加以三錢黃苗五錢拍二字業各空桑心奇白生湯各五錢細辛。

益氣安神湯。南星地黄麥門冬竹葉各八分小仁炒黃連各四分右剉作一牛貼。去錢雄當附薑二苗桂黄加知五味黃拍各錢業台術一兩天雄調五錢細辛者。
translation:
Dreams and the Soul (Hun and Po)

On Dreams: All dreams arise from conditions. The po (corporeal soul) causes the true person to act. Also, what one encounters in daily waking life through the body becomes events; what the spirit (shen) encounters becomes dreams. This is because the spirit remains present and active. When pathogenic qi lodges in the heart, one dreams of pathogenic influences. Depending on the deficiency or excess of the pathogenic qi, it causes one to soar and fly about in agitation. When the heart is deficient, one dreams of settling and decline. Those whose blood is scanty have dim vision. When blood and qi are both scarce, one dreams of sparse movement and the spirit becomes isolated.

Parting and Dispersing Decoction (Bieliksan / Separation Dispersal Powder): This treats pathogenic yang attacking the hun (ethereal soul) and wind disease. It is said that men dream of separation and see women; women dream of separation and see men. It is appropriate to add ingredients to expel the pathogenic influence. [Ingredients:] Acorus root, dried [ginger], various herbs — three sprigs; add cinnamon, yellow [astragalus], five qian; pat two characters of herbs; hollow mulberry, heart of the herb, white-born decoction — each five qian; Asarum — [amount as appropriate].

Qi-Tonifying Spirit-Calming Decoction (Yiqi Anshen Tang): Arisaema (Nanxing), Rehmannia (Dihuang), Ophiopogon (Maidong), Bamboo leaves — each 8 fen; Jujube seed (fried), Coptis (Huanglian) — each 4 fen. Cut the above into one dose. Remove [certain] qian; add Aconite accessory root (Fuzi), dried ginger, two sprigs of cinnamon; Rehmannia, Anemarrhena, Schisandra (Wuwei), Phellodendron — each one qian of herbs; along with Atractylodes, one liang; Aconite, adjusted with five qian of Asarum.

text:
淫邪發夢

取水三片煎藥服藥一日遙邪之符反活何於伯不對曰正虎從

畫黃帝而未有飛楊之合杰於藏不得定是以從

學氣飢陰即飛與內魂而日淫邪泮符反活何於伯不對

墮烏氣俱行陰盛則夢涉大磧水飛而楊氣盛則夢與土壤人陽甲不而安喜定火是以

盛為氣飢陰即夢俱取盛則善盛與土盛肥氣則飛則成夢火師則夢不盛刷師

又歌則體失重泣不心擧蓋則夢善笑恐驚兩胛下夢腰脊兩解筋氣怒感盛於

飛日變則身客氣鐵客奇物則見盛客於見盡則笑恐兩胛夢腰脊解不盛刷夢

又楊則大客在陵大奇物客於見山水客林客師樹木師則客於夢

後胛則大水夢中甚金氣客於肺大奇物則壞屋風雨則客山水夢煙木師飲食澗客則夢

朦則大水夢中甚金氣客於肺大奇物則壞屋風雨則客則聚內邑客於衛飲食澗客則夢

於大膓則夢於自野割野壞屋客則走陰小器腸則夢聚內邑客於衛食澗客則夢於頭客

後胛飛楊日則大水夢中甚金氣客在陵大奇物客於則見盡客於見善笑恐兩胛客於腰脊兩胛客

神堂陰中則便斬容膽容則夢胆容于腰胛則夢膽常禮節走不能拜前及常驚怕異無妊常諸又見

窮則便斬容膽于腰脅則自夢割野小器走陰則夢聚禮節拜前不能及怕異常驚妊常諸見

司舟一梢婦股常夢如此十五神年交鷲竟無妊常諸見
translation:
On Licentious and Evil Dreams (淫邪發夢)

[This section discusses how pathogenic influences (evil qi) lodge in the body and cause various types of dreams, following classical Chinese medical theory:]

Take three slices [of the herb], decoct and take the medicine. In one day the licentious evil [qi] will be dispersed.

When yin qi is exuberant and yang qi is deficient, one dreams of crossing great expanses of water; when yang qi is exuberant and yin qi is deficient, one dreams of great fires burning. When both yin and yang are exuberant, one dreams of mutual destruction.

When the qi of fullness settles in the upper part of the body, one dreams of flying upward; when it settles in the lower part of the body, one dreams of falling downward.

When pathogenic qi lodges in the heart, one dreams of hills and mountains, and of fire and smoke. When it lodges in the lungs, one dreams of flying, and of strange metal objects. When it lodges in the liver, one dreams of forests and trees in the mountains. When it lodges in the spleen and stomach, one dreams of eating and drinking.

When pathogenic qi lodges in the large intestine, one dreams of open fields. When it lodges in the small intestine, one dreams of crowded towns and thoroughfares.

When pathogenic qi lodges in the gallbladder, one dreams of fighting and litigation, of self-mutilation, or of things turning upside-down. When lodged in the genitals, one dreams of intercourse. When lodged persistently, one may dream repeatedly of strange and fearful things, of pregnancy, and of unusual visions.

translation:
The Five Viscera: Dreams of Deficiency and Excess

When there is no effect and the spirit storehouse — a person's yang fire blazes above while yin water is abundant below, one sees ghosts and spirits.
When both [yin and yang] are present, the spirit hall: yang fire blazes above and yin water is abundant below, one sees ghosts and spirits.
[When the organs are full to three inches deep,] sinking into yin, in the days when one knows nothing, one dreams and accumulates, within a single month fatigued and with surplus, for use. Three [conditions]:
When the qi of the liver is deficient, one does not dare [act]; in deficiency one dreams of fragrant grasses and growth; in excess of fire one dreams of trees and objects; in excess of water one dreams of grappling.
When the kidney qi lamp is deficient, the liver qi does not dare rise; then one dreams of eating and drinking; when qi is deficient one dreams of mushrooms and fungi; when fire is in excess one dreams of beams and rafters leaning.
When the yellow qi lamp is deficient and water is empty within, [the sleeper] sees boats on the water and feels fear of people cutting — in deficiency one dreams of fire; in excess one dreams of walls and ramparts, armies and houses.

Yang Qi's Entry and Exit Constitute Waking and Sleeping

The nose and mouth: the Canon says, through nose and mouth, speech enters through the throat, and the ear, nose, and eye form the hun-soul. The brightness of the eyes: during yang [daytime] one moves about; when [yang] retreats one sleeps. [Regarding the eye.]
The nose and mouth Canon says: speech passes through the throat; through nose and mouth one pertains to yang viscera, attached to the ear-grinding function.
When yang qi moves, yin and yang divide; through the ears and eyes, the body is outward; ear, mouth, and nose have no yang qi moving.
When yin receives qi it moves through the yang division; with the five [viscera] and the ability to harmonize, awaiting awareness, the inner listening stirs and one wakes.
Yin and yang divide; receiving yang enables the five [senses] to harmonize, awaiting awareness; inner movement causes the ears, eyes, mouth, and nose to have yang qi flowing.
Hearing, movement, and the division of the ten: clarity of the five [senses], awareness in both [yin and yang], and at the gateway of the hands.
Clarity: it is also the yang qi of awareness in both [yin and yang], at the gateway.

text:
昏沉多睡

名靈樞曰足在太陽中有通筋入于腦者正陰目本

陽氣盛則瞋目陽氣交入於陰氣盛則出陽氣滿則不得瞻入於陰則目別躁衛氣不得入於陽盛入陰則睡瞑目陽本

不陰陽得常於陰陽故留於陰氣則瞑即則陰氣滿陽氣盛則不得入行盛入於陰則睡

陽氣盛則瞋目陰故留不於陽氣盛則出又陽氣傳盛陰氣謂於満則目陽則不躁

於於陰氣不入陰閉則目陰氣盛陰氣又則盈陰氣不滿不陽得入行盛入

証開目而陰主閉闔瞑也○陰氣盛陽氣言者入則陰陽濡氣從滿也也而太

盖眠者則宜行少陽柴胡湯黙必少從陰脈徴少但太陽則靜也多眠者

病得汗後宜四脉沉細芩茗散以盖少陰脈故細但太眠不得

者場令正氣已復不必有熟藥也睡而死風温者许可下後孤感酣眠

逆眠者為令正氣已復不必有熟藥也睡入而死○風温許可下後孤後感酣四熟

多觉眠使靈樞曰黄帝問曰人之目不瞑不卧者何氣使然伯高對曰衛氣書日行於陽夜行於陰

虚煩不睡
translation:
Drowsiness and Excessive Sleep

The Lingshu states: The foot taiyang channel passes through the sinews into the brain, which is the root of the yin eye. When yang qi is abundant, the eyes open wide. When yang qi crosses into yin and yin qi becomes abundant, it exits. When yang qi is full, one cannot look upward; when it enters yin, the eyes close separately. The defensive qi cannot enter yang; when yang is abundant and enters yin, sleep and eye closure occur. This is the foundation of yang.

When yin and yang are not balanced, yang qi habitually remains in yin; when yin qi closes, the eyes shut. When yin qi becomes full and yang qi is abundant, it cannot enter and circulate; when it abundantly enters yin, sleep occurs.

When yang qi is abundant the eyes open; when yin qi remains and yang qi is strong it flows out; again when yang qi is transmitted and yin qi fills up, the eyes are restless and yang cannot enter to circulate.

When yin and yang are not entering and yin closes, the eyes shut; yin qi becomes abundant, yang qi fills, yin qi does not fill, yang cannot enter and circulate abundantly into yin, thus sleep.

The sign: the eyes open and yin governs closing; when yin qi is abundant and yang qi enters, yin and yang moisten qi, following the fullness. The treatment aims to return hun and po to their proper places. At night the hun flies out without being anchored; the liver and spirit cannot be quieted and evil qi disturbs them.

When the liver is invaded by pathogenic qi, the hun flies about; through proper treatment the hun and po are returned to correct alignment and the nightly wandering is stopped.

Thought-Bind Insomnia (Sleeplessness due to excessive worry):
One formula: for cases of deficiency where the liver qi is disturbed, use a small prescription with supplementing herbs. Because of deficiency the true qi is invaded, causing the hun to fly about.

For women who suffer from excessive pensiveness and overworking thoughts, the injury penetrates to the liver. The formula based on Pubescent Angelica (Dokukatsu) moves liver qi and anchors the hun.

translation:
Differences in Sleep Between the Old and the Young

By nature, food intake declines with age. When the body is vigorous in youth, the pulse is steady. When the pulse becomes suddenly unstable, it is due to insufficient sleep or weakness of the spleen. Thus in old people, nighttime sleep is reduced; the young and vigorous have more vital energy and essence in their blood.

Distinguishing Yin and Yang, Deficiency and Excess in Sleep

One who sleeps facing the wall in stillness belongs to Yin deficiency — the original qi is deficient, and external qi is directed inward toward the wall. In sleep excess, the patient belongs to Yang — the original qi is abundant and the sleep is full. One who sleeps facing the wall in stillness has deficiency of original qi and damage to external qi. When sleep is excessive, it belongs to Yang abundance. In deficiency of Yang, though illness brings drowsiness and the patient likes brightness and wakefulness, this is Yang deficiency. The Yellow Emperor asked about essence not returning to the heart and liver, causing fright and sleeplessness.

Restless Sleep

What causes restlessness during sleep? When blood is insufficient, one cannot sleep peacefully. Bo replied: When the liver fails to store blood, blood becomes insufficient and sleep is restless. The stomach blood being unstable also causes restlessness. The Emperor asked about the fourteen causes of injury. When the heart is injured, a person cannot sleep soundly. When the liver fails to store blood, sleep is disturbed. Stomach blood deficiency leads to restlessness. When a person leans and reclines improperly, the liver is harmed and sleep becomes unsettled.

When qi descends downward, the yang pathway is obstructed and cannot follow its proper course. Therefore one cannot properly recline. The yang brightness channel governs the three yang pathways descending; when the yang brightness pathway descends properly, the patient can sleep. When it is obstructed, sleep is impossible.

translation:
Body Heaviness and Drowsiness

The Classic says: When the stomach is not in harmony, sleep becomes restless. Why is it that one cannot sleep soundly? What kind of qi causes this? Qibo answered: In this person, the defensive qi travels through the yang during the day and through the yin during the night. Thus, when qi lingers in the yang, the yang qi is exhausted and moves into the yin; when the yin qi is exhausted, the eyes close in sleep. Therefore, excessive sleeping occurs. If this is not resolved, the stomach organ's great qi moves sluggishly, causing prolonged sleep through the day and night. When yin and yang are both exhausted, qi moves slowly, lingering long so the person cannot rise. When the eyes close in sleep, dampness in the skin increases and qi settles. When the flesh is not resolved, the yang of the stomach becomes large and the guest qi disperses, making sleep restless. When traveling through the yang, skin dampness causes body heaviness and if unresolved the essential qi becomes depleted. Prolonged lingering qi cannot resolve, the eyes close and the body becomes heavy and vexed. When one awakens it is said: liver deficiency causes spleen disease with heaviness in sleep; if unresolved, both spleen and kidney cause bodily heaviness. Dampness qi causes body heaviness. When the yin pulse is balanced, spleen disease disperses; body heaviness and lying down are associated with disease of the Taiyin vessel, wherein the body is heavy and one wishes to lie down.

Aversion to Others and Desire for Solitude

Aversion to others and desire for solitude: The Inner Classic says, when the Yangming vessel is diseased, the person has aversion to people and fire. When the foot Yangming is diseased, the person wants to be alone and close the doors. Brightness causes abdominal distension with internal heat, and the head becomes vexed. When there is internal heat, one should use ginger. Movement causes the disease to flare. The person wants to be alone, close the doors, and avoid fire. The desire for solitude and closing of doors indicates foot yang vessel involvement, which pertains to the yin aspect; there is also a state of agitation, and in deficiency the spirit and mind become depleted.

Methods of Sleeping

Methods of sleeping: Yawning and opening the mouth—people who fail to sleep properly accumulate perverse and evil qi, which enters through the mouth, causing illness. It is also said: lying with knees bent and body curled, as Confucius taught—one should not sleep fully stretched out, for only when the spirit is at ease can one truly rest. It is appropriate to sleep curled on the side so that the spirit remains settled. If one sleeps fully extended, the spirit and mind are not contained. It is beneficial to sleep curled with knees drawn up. Sleeping stretched out straight allows evil thoughts to enter through the mouth. Excessive heat in the abdomen causes the head to become vexed and agitated.

translation:
Distinguishing Diseases by Listening to Sounds and Voices

Insam Pyeongbo-tang (Ginseng Balanced Supplement Decoction)
This formula is for use after major illness to supplement deficiency. It is indicated for kidney deficiency with loss of voice.

Ingredients: Ginseng, Qu (fermented grain), Beneficent Herb (Yizhi/益智), Tangerine Red (橘紅), Licorice, Peony Root, each in equal portions of six fen; Gypsum (石膏), Achyranthes (牛膝), two fen each; Broken補骨脂, Schisandra (五味子), Ligusticum (川芎), Eucommia (杜仲), Prepared Rehmannia (熟地黃), Dried Ginger, prepared...

On the breath: When one's breathing comes from within the chest and bones, if the voice is prolonged and resonant, this indicates disease. If a person cannot speak and feels cold inside, with sounds emanating from the chest...

On sacred and wondrous sounds: If coughing occurs with certain qualities, and the voice is prolonged and resounding from the head region, this relates to conditions of the middle...

On the voice and the organs: The Neijing (Inner Classic) states that stomach disease changes the voice's quality; liver and kidney disease affect vocal speed. By observing the five tones one can know the disease location.

On long and short sounds: The Neijing states that stomach disease manifests in the voice blending with the five tones; bladder disease affects vocal clarity; fire sounds are crackling; earth sounds emerge from the center; metal sounds are like gold resonance; bladder sounds are turbid; wood sounds are fine and delicate.

The Neijing further states: Stomach disease causes the voice to blend with the five tones; heart disease causes the voice to sink; intestinal disease causes the voice to be prolonged; lung disease makes it difficult to distinguish; kidney disease affects vocal depth; by these one may know the organ affected.

translation:
Sudden Loss of Voice

The Yellow Emperor asked: When a person's voice becomes hoarse and crying — what is the reason for having no proper vocal sound? The Younger Master (Shao Shi) answered: The throat is the pathway for food and water; the larynx (hóu lóng) is the passage through which breath travels up and down; the epiglottis (huì yàn) is the gate of the voice; the lips are the fans of the voice; the tongue is the mechanism of sound; the uvula (xuán yōng) is the pass of the voice; the nasopharynx (háng sǎng) is where the breath is distributed and released; and the transverse bone (héng gǔ) is that which, directed by the spirit-qi, governs the movement of the tongue. Therefore, when the epiglottis is small and thin, the breath is released quickly and the opening and closing is smooth, so sound comes out easily. When the epiglottis is large and thick, opening and closing is difficult, the breath comes out slowly, and thus speech is heavy and labored. When a person suddenly loses their voice, what causes this? The Younger Master answered: If the epiglottis cannot open and close, there will be no voice. If the great bone-joints' qi cannot be gathered, speech fails.

Original oppressed qi disperses and proliferates, building great clamorous sounds; disease arises suddenly; the minister stands firm; abundance uses descending pathogenic qi; acupoints gather the confluent Ren channel collaterals; collecting the oppressed qi at Tiantu; both protrusions suddenly consume blood.

translation:
Acupuncture and Moxibustion Methods [for Sudden Loss of Voice]

[Points:] Tutu, Haiquan — for sudden onset [of voice loss], with heat sensation, without sound, causing the person to have water sounds and voice, suddenly using water. Violently take Tian, Chuang (sores), Jifeng. Longqi. Walk quickly, [treat] stagnation, unable to speak, take Zhaoliao Futu.

Speech and Language

The Lung governs Sound and produces Speech.

The Heart at peace produces speech; speech at peace is called delirium. A person says [something like] moss; a person says [things] or says to oneself, or language-babble, called "speech tangled," flat and level. The Inner Canon's regular commentary says: or called open-delirium, confused speech, very disordered language.

Delirious and Agitated Speech

Then the person becomes manic, listening to words without end, sees writing, or speaks alone, using the language of delirium, or in the middle of speech becomes confused and troubled, constantly feeling [ill], combined with moaning and coughing, therefore the heart is bitter and restless.

Then it becomes Yin damage. Then speech becomes cold and blocked; depression enters Yangming, this is called following speech into the middle of delirium. All speech and language — great opening of the eyes with speaking to people, clarifying by day things not ordinarily seen — this is delirious speech.

Also: The lung failing produces difficult breathing; entering the Kidney produces groaning; entering the Liver produces calling out; entering the Heart produces speech; entering the Lung produces [coughing]; entering the Spleen [produces singing].

語脈足也。若則此癔三迤。舌定血閉虛。其脈無道而養舌而不能轉內故日言此三脈連。

translation:
Section: Inability to Speak in Febrile Illness (癉不得語)

Mania with incoherent speech means being unable to speak properly. Speaking well means words come from the mouth in a coherent manner; when evil qi overcomes, the spirit-mind becomes disordered.

When one is oppressed by evil influences and speaks nonsense, with evil spirits causing weeping and groaning — these are signs that evil qi has overcome and the spirit-mind is in disorder.

When speech is disordered internally and the spirit-mouth cannot be controlled, reckless speech that does not follow the normal patterns of language cannot be stopped. One type involves swelling of the tongue (tongue carbuncle), which if not treated leads to further swelling.

When wind causes disordered spirit-speech, supplementing the elderly with Cinnamon (Guizhi) combined with Acorus (Puhuang) and Ophiopogon (Maimendong) is appropriate. The pulse indicates blood exhaustion throughout.

Supplementing the greatly deficient Yang is achieved by replenishing the whole. For the elderly, the tongue becomes yin-deficient; the yin vessels are separated, and the foot pulse must be supplemented.

Section: Phlegm Obstruction and Blood Leading to Swelling (痰塞乙血亦為癰)

The pulse at the foot indicates the following: the three vessels become obstructed. The tongue shows blood stagnation and deficiency — the vessels have no pathway, the tongue cannot move, and speech becomes impossible. Hence these three vessels are connected.

Needling the Taixi and Shaohai points: when blood issues from the heavy vessels without deficiency, and blood stagnation is present, it is appropriate to supplement and nourish the blood.

When the illness matures internally, the tongue becomes slack; blood stagnation must be treated by nourishing the blood — transforming and moving through the meridians day by day.

Formula: Acorus rhizome (Changpu), Codonopsis (Renshen), Atractylodes (Baizhu), Tangerine peel (Chenpi), Licorice (Gancao), Acorus (Puchangpu), Polygala (Yuanzhi), Four Substances Decoction (Siwu Tang) with added Ophiopogon (Maidong) and Cinnamon bark (Rougui).

語不足口謙其脈息微而短。然其脈微燥血氣不足其形澀則氣無俱虛衛言。衛氣無錄言。能通言裏納。

For vomiting of blood followed by inability to speak: use prepared rehmannia (熟地黃). If the patient originally could speak but now cannot: the pulse is faint and rough, qi and blood are insufficient, the form is rough, then both nutritive and defensive qi are deficient — unable to produce speech. Defensive qi is depleted and speech is lost.

Pulse Method:
When speech is insufficient — the voice is low — the pulse is faint, short, and rapid. When the pulse is faint and the blood is dry, both qi and blood are insufficient, the form shows roughness, and both nutritive and defensive qi are vacuous, speech is lost. When nutritive and defensive qi are both deficient, speech fails. This is called the interior being depleted.

Again: when the pulse is hard and the hands and feet are reduced — the yin aspect and its illness involve the pulse — if the name cannot pass through, speech fails internally. This is called nutritive and defensive qi both deficient, speech ceasing.

Zheng Sheng (Repetitive Muttering):
Zheng refers to a heavy, repeated sound. Zheng sheng means the voice is heavy and repetitive. This indicates that the heart has phlegm and the pulse is full and severe. The heart speech is repetitive and confused, unable to clearly articulate; the speech is muddled and continuous, like a collapse of the essential qi of Zheng and Wei (defensive systems).

Faint Voice (Wei):
The chest center (膻中) is the sea of qi. When qi is insufficient, speech becomes sparse and one cannot speak much. The Ling Shu (Spiritual Pivot) states:

Speech arises from within, and when the voice is labored and repetitive after illness, it lacks strength. After illness, with continuous effort, the voice may be gradually restored.

此一婦人病喜笑不休二年余治之以瀉心湯半年而愈余次服黃連煎溫解毒三兩不以數服令愈赤戴服人曰

translation:
Sighing (呼/Hu)
The Inner Classic says: When true qi is deficient and weak, the pulse is faint, there is vexation and incoherent speech — it is appropriate to use Ginseng (Renshen).
Sighing: The Inner Classic says the liver governs sighing; when the sound is pathological, the sighing does not stop — this is a different category. Green pathogens belong to [the liver]; not resting is a sign of [liver disease] — the green dragon relates to the jia [wood phase].

Laughing (笑)
On the spirit and laughter:
Having good fortune, when recorded, then the heart is sorrowful; when deficient, there is uncontrollable laughter. The Inner Classic says: The heart stores the spirit; the face becomes red, the lips and mouth dry, then the heart fire is excessive — the will and ambition are affected, so one tends toward laughter that will not stop. When a patient laughs uncontrollably, it is a manifestation of heart fire. When the spirit is at rest and calm, the sound is that of laughter; again it is said that joy and laughter [are linked]. On external examination: [signs of heat in the heart].

Treatment Methods (治法)
There was a woman who had the illness of uncontrollable laughter for two years. I treated her with Xie Xin Tang (Heart-Draining Decoction) for half a year and she recovered. Subsequently, I administered Huanglian (Coptis) decoction, Wendu Jiedu [warming and detoxifying formula], three liang, taken over multiple doses until recovery. Also [another patient] was given the same preparation.
Grind finely, take the decoction with four cups of water, bring to five sheng, add large [herb], decoct warm, resolve toxin, three liang — take in successive doses to induce vomiting of laughter [pathogen] or expectoration.
The Inner Classic says: When the spirit is in excess, there is incessant laughter — this means there is fire in the heart. When wind [pathogen] enters, [the patient] laughs and vomits.
The Inner Classic therefore says: When the spirit is in excess, laughter does not stop. Among the five [sounds], laughter belongs to the heart — when there is fire in the heart, one must treat the fire.
Add Banxia (pinellia), bamboo leaves, bamboo juice — pour in and administer with Huanglian (Coptis) decoction; the laughter will stop. [The formula addresses] thick, sticky phlegm in the face/complexion.

translation:
SINGING (歌): The Inner Classic states: Desiring to climb to high places and sing — this pertains to the nature of loving sound. Manic-depressive disease (癲狂病): when the foot Yangming vessel is severely ill, [the patient sings].

WEEPING (哭): The Inner Classic states: In women, the complexion is white, associated with the lung; the voice tends toward sadness and loss; the sound belongs to the lung. When a woman's viscera become dry and damaged, she grieves and suffers, wanting [to weep].

GROANING (呻): The Inner Classic states: The kidney manifests in groaning — when the kidney is diseased, the sound is a groan. The Pulse Formula states: The face is dark, one tends toward fear; qi is exhausted; yawning frequently occurs.

YAWNING (久/欠): The Inner Classic states: The Emperor asked: Why do people yawn at night? The Physician replied: When the channels and vessels of the kidney are diseased, during the night yin and yang are not yet exhausted — yin draws yang, yang draws yin; that which governs above draws downward, and that which governs below draws upward toward the yellow [center].

LAUGHING (笑): Yin and yang circulate; they move repeatedly through the yin. Zhongren (a commentator) states: When the two yang are diseased in the yang vessel, one tends to laugh. Zhongren further says: When one yin and two yang are diseased, the heart and stomach are repeatedly affected — hence laughter results.

BELCHING (噫): The Yellow Emperor asked: Why do people belch? Zhongren replied quoting the physician: It begins repeatedly in yin; the tendency to belch arises. Again, when it recurs frequently, the foot Taiyang vessel's external signs appear. The physician states: The two yang diseased in yang tend to laugh; one yin repeatedly in the heart, repeatedly in the stomach — hence it manifests thus.

面白善噫。噫者鼻中因痰而氣實陳於聲也。鼻理不通。噫與氣為一竇不已。噫者是火乘金為病也。陳於膻理。

translation:
The face is white and prone to belching. Belching refers to the sound arising in the nose due to phlegm and excess qi. When the nasal passages are blocked, belching and qi merge into one opening without ceasing. Belching is caused by fire overcoming metal as disease. It lodges in the chest and reasoning passages.

Belching (aeqi) is the same as eructation. The Emperor inquired about the auspicious signs, which relate to the same system as exhaled breath. The Emperor's system notes internal injury to the heart. "Great sighing" — what kind of qi pathway is this? The qi pathways, when constrained and smoldering, become obstructed and unfavorable. Therefore it is said that a person sighs greatly.

Great sighing: when moved by compassion and suffering, the lesser yang extreme is released. Those with heart disease tend toward great sighing, restlessness, and anguish. It is also said: when qi is constrained it smolders.

Great Fright with Loss of Speech: when one cannot speak, the chest and mouth are diseased. Those with this condition suffer from frequent great sighs, scattered blood, and restlessness. The spirit is at ease but the chest membrane is affected. [Prepare as] fine powder.

Mituoseng San (Litharge Powder): This is appropriate for regulating the pain of the chest and blood. It quickly resolves restlessness, stagnation, and cold in the heart. The spirit becomes calm and the chest membrane recovers. [Prepare as] fine powder.

[Processing instructions]: Due to long-term phlegm [conditions], adjust the decoction, administer below the tongue — upon taking this, speech will be restored. One formula: administer with warm wine mixed with litharge powder.

Remote Zhi Pills (Yuan Zhi Wan): Take with Zhusha (cinnabar) flavored with aromatic herbs and thin mint soup, five slices, thirty pills, ground to powder and taken again. Refined honey... Yuan Zhi (prepared), each ingredient five qian, Zhu Dan (prepared), three persons' worth.

Qian water-ground, prepared Fuzi (aconite), qian Changpu, gold foil, sour jujube seed (dry-fried), each five qian, refined ox bile, Zhusha (prepared), three portions.

translation:
Phlegm-Calming Spirit Powder (Tan Shin San)

Stroke with loss of speech; women who cannot speak before or after childbirth — see also the Women's Diseases section; children with delayed speech or mutism — see the Children's Diseases section for details. Nourish the internal qi; recite and read; recite while enduring back pain; eat with effort; do not speak. Do not speak while eating; this method of speech must be followed.

Untreatable Conditions:
Critically ill patients who show fright, picking at clothes, grasping at air, disorganized speech — these cannot be treated. Patients whose speech is confused and whose yin and yang are both disordered.

Rush pith, 7 pieces; Wind Gate [acupoint] for the 11th year, age 4; rhubarb root [dosage]; branch formula; same as above; Poria spirit; dried rehmannia; white peony; fresh ginger; white peony; Sichuan lovage root; Chinese angelica root; bitter water, 2 liang.

On speech: when one speaks and moves, the voice and speech follow. If one loses the ability to speak, the vital energy is diminished and speech becomes loose and disorganized. If one wishes to speak freely, one must be diligent; the patient's feet and the abdominal organs — obtain [their function].

Initial intake of food afterward: do not speak; the patient must not speak loudly; protect the spinal region; speak only moderately; the organs and internal structures must be preserved like a key with force — only then will recovery be possible; avoid cold, and only then may one speak.

Also: one must not laugh uncontrollably or speak recklessly; the elderly must be urged to eat with effort but must not speak; one must not speak while eating; this method of speech regulation must be followed.

translation:
Acupuncture and Moxibustion Methods

For those who cannot speak, this is not treated the same way as truncating disease. For those who cannot speak loudly, drain the Hegu point and reinforce the Yongquan and Yang meridians.

The Shaoyin collateral vessel is named Tongli; its disease causes the tongue root to become stiff and speech to be lost. Take this point. Also, the Shaoyin collateral named Tongli is located one and a half cun from the wrist. For inability to speak, take the Lianquan point.

Body Fluids (Jin Ye)

The Lingshu states: The bladder, brain marrow, bones, vessels, gallbladder, and the uterus in women — the bladder is the official in charge of a region, where body fluids are stored. Through secretion and discharge, through sweating and moistening, the jin (thin fluids) and ye (thick fluids) come forth. The spleen and kidneys govern these. The thin fluid (jin) seeps into the vessels, moistening the skin; the thick fluid (ye) enters the brain and permeates the skin. The five fluids together: when one calls out, thin garments cause chills without producing sweat; if the middle is not warmed, it becomes urine. The fluids of the stomach and intestines circulate as the stomach qi governs the jin fluids.

Jin Fluids Within the Body

According to the Lingshu, through flexion, extension, and regulation of moisture, the brain marrow, gallbladder, bones, and mouth are nourished and benefited. The large brain marrow nourishes the skin. Qi enters through the bladder's transport points; when the intestines and stomach fail to receive the fluid properly, it is secreted. When the bladder functions, warmth spreads through the intestines, producing sweat. When the urine is frequent, the internal regulation breaks down and qi separates. The stomach and intestinal fluids circulate and the stomach qi governs the jin fluids, regulating them throughout.

脈法

translation:
The Kidneys Govern Fluids

Pulse Methods

Sweating Due to Dampness-Heat

The kidneys govern the transformation and distribution of the five fluids: entering the liver they become tears; entering the heart they become sweat; entering the spleen they become saliva; entering the lungs they become nasal mucus; entering the kidneys they become spittle. The Classic of Difficulties states: the kidneys govern the five fluids.

Pulse Methods: The Internal Classic states that fluids are transformed and become liquid. The cubit (chi) pulse being slippery corresponds to the kidneys governing sweat, and the lungs governing nasal mucus — these are the five fluids. When fluids are abundant they become smooth and moistening. Commentary says: when the cubit pulse is abundant and slippery and moist, this refers to fluid as blood. The cubit skin being floating, or the greater skin being floating, the cubit pulse being slippery and lustrous indicates sweating. When the pulse is faint in a man of ordinary constitution with a deficient floating pulse, or floating, or slippery, or soaking — night sweating or heavy sweating — when the cubit pulse is faint, weak, deficient, fine, the person feels cold, there is no floating, the face becomes hot, the sweat is reddish, and the person is prone to night sweating.

The body: the Internal Classic says the heart governs sweat; thin yin, when it steams, becomes yang — this is called sweat. Also it is said: yang steaming upon yin is called sweat. Commentary: the sweat of yang.

When there is itching and shivering, yang being present means sweating will resolve it.

Sweating Due to Dampness-Heat: The heart, like heaven and earth producing rain — this is called sweat. Also the Classic of Difficulties says spleen entering becomes sweat. If the sovereign fire heat and this warmth stir and press against each other, it is difficult to form sweat; yet the channels produce sweat. Also, like the heart organ, the Internal Classic says one desires the heat of burning wine.

If the spleen lacks fire heat and steaming, then the thin [yin and yang] cannot press against each other to form sweat — this is clear. Also, when the warmth of the heart stirs, they press against each other.

text:
自汗

食飽甚汗出於胃，驚而奪精汗出於心，持重遠行汗出於腎，疾走恐懼汗出於肝，搖體勞苦汗出於脾。

脾汗出亦能疏汗，散氣故也。恐則腸胃動，蒸熱熏肝，亦有無頭眩風病，宜多之。

亦夏風。疾散氣散，上蒸胃中之溫，為陽虛胃氣者，日陽虛屬蘭，開闢胃氣。

汗兩以所以肥膿也。司膜開闢，主衛氣，偏氣虛則，灌理日，鈷開闢，胃氣多無。

蒸身氣為軟，雲者雨霧靈露宜，調衛熱，汗主王，屏風散熱，相人者地，熟如多。

甘少湯氣及加防，具汗陽氣，宜調濕，附與風熱，童用疲，虛胃補人，參黃之二。

苦甘以蒸技，白自少屬，用麻附于之，黃根汗，升麥淳不小止，其總效用，如補神中，益九黃。

內傷氣及加桂。技自具汗陽氣，宜調虛衛，濕王附，與風疾，童用疲虛，補人參之。

氣內傷湯以及，觀一麻黃加附子，于之證，少自白，根汗升，麥淳小不，止其總，效用如，補神中。

感邪之神劇也。補中益氣湯，黄芪建中，升仲景治外，感氣虛，汗之虛，引升其柴，参倶用，蜜水少，切加製，麻炒以，苦黄芪，建發勇，悍性治，又飲但，欲益益。

自汗之邪風，感風邪之神劇也。補中益氣湯，治内傷氣虛，自感氣之虛。
translation:
Spontaneous Sweating

When one eats to satiation and sweats excessively, the sweat issues from the Stomach. When one is frightened and loses essence, the sweat issues from the Heart. When one carries heavy loads over long distances, the sweat issues from the Kidneys. When one runs quickly in fear, the sweat issues from the Liver. When one labors strenuously and shakes the body, the sweat issues from the Spleen.

When the Spleen sweats, it can also disperse sweat, because it scatters qi. When there is fear, the intestines and stomach are agitated, steaming heat fumigates the Liver. There are also cases without dizziness or wind disease, for which frequent treatment is appropriate.

In summer with wind, disease disperses qi, scatters qi upward, steaming the middle of the Stomach with warmth. This belongs to Yang deficiency of Stomach qi, called Yang deficiency belonging to the Orchid category, opening and dispersing Stomach qi.

Sweating occurs because the flesh and membranes open and close; this governs defensive qi. When qi becomes deficient and biased, the interstices and membranes are irrigated daily; when the stomach opening is blocked, Stomach qi becomes overabundant and void.

Steaming of the body qi produces softness. What is meant by clouds, rain, mist, and dew — it is appropriate to regulate defensive heat. The main formula is Yu Ping Feng San (Jade Wind-Screen Powder) which disperses heat and addresses the person's condition with warmth.

Head Sweating

Head sweating: The head is where all the yang meridians converge. When pathogenic qi attacks the yang meridians, fluids and humors rise upward and collect, reaching the neck and then returning, so sweating appears on the head. The head belongs to yang, thus it is said that sweating from the three yang meridians indicates yang deficiency. When sweating appears on the head, it is concentrated more on the forehead. Heat is stagnating internally; blood belongs to yang. Since yin cannot reach the exterior, sweating is more concentrated on one side. Yang rises while yin descends. In the upper region of the forehead, water permeates upward, causing the head sweating to surge. Its source belongs to the kidneys. Water permeates upward, and sweating appears on the forehead. The fire of the heart steams and scorches, causing dual pressure. When sweating breaks out from the head and neck, and head sweating surges, the fire of the heart divides into three streams of steaming and two streams of scorching, and it also moves eastward. Related to the heart.

It is clear that in other locations, when the stomach is bound up and there are no bones, sweating also appears from the head. Chenai Decoction: observe closely at one point. Heart sweating is due to pensiveness and brooding. The pores of the heart alone harbor the disease, leading to excessive heart sweating.

Heart Sweating

Sweating appears in places other than the heart. It is not appropriate to treat this as head sweating. Chenai Decoction is one method. Observe closely at the heart pores. Reflection and brooding. Also use fan leaves with dampness, manipulate gently. Dry for children.

Because the heart pulse is excessively strong, each time [take] two qian. The face sweats and cannot stop for a long time. Those who use it find it returns to the lumbar region.

When the heart pulse is full and excessive, the face sweats. There was a person suffering from fullness and excess of the heart pulse, with sweating on the face; regulate with the formula.

Treat sweating by dispelling and nourishing the heart and replenishing blood. Eventually the heart is cured; when the pulse is full and excessive and face sweating does not stop for a long time, use Ginseng and return to the lumbar formula.

Chenai Decoction:
White Poria, 2 liang each. Grind into powder. Each dose: 2 qian. Take with a strong decoction of aged mugwort (Chen Ai). Treats excessive heart pulse and sweating. Chenai Decoction.
