Collapse of Yang Syndrome (亡陽證)

Yang is what can be treated. When sweating is profuse and does not stop, the face turns pale (greenish), the chest and diaphragm are affected, and sweating cannot be controlled — this indicates the True Yang is nearly collapsed, which is why it is called Collapse of Yang, treated with warming methods.

When there is deficiency and the exterior is not firm, sweating is inevitable, causing palpitations and unceasing sweating.

The Yang Decoction is used when sweating leads to collapse, with profuse sweating, irritability, fluid leakage, cold intolerance, loss of fluids — the True Yang is nearly collapsed and difficult to treat; hence the various Yang-restoring formulas including Guizhi Fuzi Tang (Cinnamon Twig and Aconite Decoction).

Guizhi Fuzi Tang (Cinnamon Twig and Aconite Decoction):
Cinnamon twig 2 qian, Roasted licorice 1 piece, water decoction; right dose divided; roasted aconite, white atractylodes, each 3 fen — take as an emergency formula.

Method to Stop Sweating (止汗法):
Use powdered substances applied to the navel to fill and stop sweating; divide into portions; for strengthening Yang, use moxibustion; apply medicated fumigation with red powder preparations and other herbal combinations.

Warming Powder (溫粉):
Dragon bone powder, oyster shell powder — applied externally to stop sweating; applied over the whole body. Note: mistaken use of glutinous rice with yellow powder is cautioned against.

Schizonepeta, Ligusticum chuanxiong 1 liang, Angelica dahurica, and other herbs equal parts — wrap in cotton, apply/rub over the body, and take orally as powder.

Ingredients: Halloysitum rubrum (red kaolin) and Os Draconis (dragon bone), 1 liang each; Ephedra root and oyster shell powder, 1 liang each; cotton powder and alum, 1 liang each. Pound and sift into a fine powder. Mix evenly with an appropriate liquid and apply.

Mix evenly with salt and apply. Use Galla chinensis (Chinese gallnut), cotton powder, alum. Pound and sift into powder. Mix with an appropriate liquid and apply.

No Sweating (Muham)
[Discussion of conditions involving absence of sweating, blood in sweat, accumulation of pus and blood, and various named conditions:]
In summer, when the body's yang qi is depleted and cannot be stopped, in conditions where the exterior is excess and there is no sweating, the sweat does not occur. When yin is deficient and yang is excess on the exterior, no sweating occurs. When yin flows outward through the exterior, yang is deficient internally and sweating does not stop.

If true yang qi is solid and the condition does not resolve for a long time, in cold damage affecting the interior there is no sweating; when yin syndrome is present, there is generally no sweating from yin. At the four seasons, when yang qi is absent, there is no sweat.

The body becomes hot and feverish; after prolonged duration, if there is excess in the yin interior, in cold damage with no sweating and mirror-like syndrome, yin counterflow occurs.

The body is like beads of [sweat] that do not flow; there is no qi, cold sweat, and the syndrome is one of yin counterflow.

Terminal Sweating (Jeol-han)
So-called terminal sweating: when [this type of] sweat emerges in the morning, death follows by evening; when it emerges in the evening, death follows by morning. When all six yang channels are exhausted, sweat comes out like beads and does not flow. Terminal sweat is sticky like oil or like threads of silk.

Soft/Cold Sweating (Yu-han)
According to Zhongjing's discussion, soft sweating emerges once and then ceases; it is sticky like oil, and accumulates day by day.

Sweating with Unfavorable Signs
These are untreatable. In cold-heat conditions, sweat appears like beads and does not dissolve — this is yin cold-heat disease.

translation:
Prohibitions and Contraindications

When head sweat appears like beads and does not flow, this means yang collapse and imminent death. When yang sweat is like oil and cold sweat flows out, the body lacks moisture.

In treating a patient, when sweat appears in such a manner, if the condition is critical and the disease cannot be treated, there is sweat; only cold damages heat disease. Spontaneous sweating has nine patterns, all of which can be treated. Cases like yin water with cold limbs indicate yang deficiency and yin excess, where the earth's yang is about to collapse; such cases where death-sweat appears must be severe.

During the winter months, heaven and earth are closed, blood and qi are stored within; even if illness occurs, it is not appropriate to induce much sweating. Spontaneous sweating: the nine pungent things.

Pungent foods such as chives and garlic — the ancient sages said: yang essence gives birth to water in the center; liquid is generated from water; yin qi is generated within; yang qi is generated within; liquid generates the central fluid.

On the Accumulation of Qi and Generation of Fluids

It is said: when yang is deficient and yin predominates, the form acts as a vessel; at the beginning, water is generated, yin qi arises, fire then consolidates it, and movement occurs within form, generating water.

It is said: fire is the origin of all things; one who first exists generates from oneself. Water as the beginning also has form; from within water, water generates.

It is said: a person's body is one — this can be verified. If poverty troubles the heart and the heart stirs, then fluids are generated; qi also having a heart can result in bland harmony.

translation:
Tears (Chapter on Tears, Difficulty of Discharge)

When the heart moves, it generates great sweating. When the heart is agitated, great yang arises. When great yang arises, water is produced. When water is produced in yang, it can be seen as tears. In the beginning, heaven and earth produce one yang, and yang produces water; water then accumulates in the yang, and this is how tears are formed.

The Zong (ancestral) vessel: the Zong vessel connects with the stomach. The liver vessel meets the Bofu (stomach). It is said: the five organs and six bowels all have their tears. The person whose tears flow — the qi of the spleen gathers and begins to move, and thus tears arise.

When the essence-spirit is agitated, the essence moves; when the essence moves, it traverses its pathway; when the pathway opens, the nasal passage opens, and fluids emerge; when fluids emerge, tears flow out of the mouth. Thus the five and six — the five organs and six bowels — are the masters of tears. When a person is sad, tears and nasal fluids come forth together.

Saliva and Fluids (Internal, Kidney Section):

The kidneys govern fluids. Fire blazing and water overabundant — when bile accumulates and the bile system ages, the bile fluid and lung fluid together form saliva. Saliva is the fluid of the lung. The membrane fat becomes mature fluid — thick or thin — and hence the Classic says: after coughing, the lung rises, and coughing follows; after coughing, the fluid is seen as flowing saliva. When the system cannot hold itself steady and cannot rise, the master descends, and the fluid pathway closes, so that fluid accumulates and the pathway is blocked; when the pathway is blocked the fluid cannot flow, and coughing with saliva results.

translation:
Three Distinctions Among Phlegm, Saliva, and Fluid Retention

Phlegm (痰) is another name for the body's fluids. From what a person eats and drinks each day, phlegm is formed. This is based on the principle that although the source is one, the manifestations differ. Phlegm is a substance — an alternative name for the body's fluids. Fluid retention (飲) also has its times of flaring and movement. They differ in how they accumulate. Fluid retention lies dormant in the stomach, following the qi upward, overflowing to the mouth and corners of the lips, flooding the lungs, causing congestion, and recurring without restraint — these are the signs of its flaring and movement.

Distinguishing Clear and Turbid Among Phlegm and Fluid

These are names for the condition. When fluids accumulate in the stomach and cannot be properly transformed, they stagnate and become disease. When water is heated and the fluids steam together, they form phlegm. Fluid that is thin and watery is called water-fluid (水飲); fluid that pools is called retained fluid (留飲); fluid that branches is called suspended fluid (支飲). Fluid that is clear in color is called clear-phlegm fluid; fluid that is thick is called turbid phlegm.

Master Wang Yinjun's Discourse on Phlegm

Ancient formulas held that phlegm arises because heart fire flares up suddenly, scorching and obstructing the earth phase (spleen), creating obstruction. Thus phlegm takes various forms: thin watery fluid, pooled fluid, stolen fluid — those that are clear in color are phlegm-fluids.

The four wind-related symptoms: dizziness, facial swelling, tinnitus, or pain, bitterness in the mouth, eye discharge and sourness, or twitching of the gums and teeth, itching and numbness of the ear rims, or floating sensations — these are all related to fluid disorders.

Swelling, pain, counterflow of wind, eye puffiness, ear sounds like an eagle's cry, qi unable to descend, color like scorched sediment, form like broken-down peach resin — [illegible]

translation:
This passage is from the Internal Medicine (Naegyeong) section of Dongui Bogam, discussing various disease manifestations and their treatments. The text describes:

Looking inward at internal conditions and their various types — such as the sensation of water stagnating below the heart, cold and soft feeling in the head with pain, or intermittent swelling and heaviness.

Along the spine and joints, there may be jaundice-like symptoms, blurred vision like looking through fog or frozen water, progressing to paralysis and weakness, or the development of habitual conditions.

There may be worms, blockages, swelling at the top of the head, nodules forming, clouding of the eyes, numbness, stiffness, coldness in the hands, pain in the shoulders, or sudden pain.

Conditions such as agitation, irritability, or heat in the head, closed passages, wind accumulation, lung abscesses, itching of the skin rashes, pain in the abdomen, or acute episodes.

Symptoms at the throat and chest — such as spitting and qi reversal — throat swellings, downward surging, epileptic conditions, flushing of the face, heat with palpitations, startling fright, and seizure-like states.

Coughing and vomiting, palpitations of the heart, fluid accumulation, water startling the mind, dizziness, convulsions.

Fluids and humors — conditions of phlegm accumulation, external and internal, water stoppage, dark fluids, fright with scorching of the lungs, fever with toxins.

Treatment principles follow regarding stagnation, small and large urination adjustments, closed and startled states, bone manipulation, drying and nourishing the liver, driving out pathogens, dispersing accumulations.

Discussion of the four and six types of fluid intake, examination of the actual condition, analysis of the mechanisms, and the methods of Zhu Danxi. Because of internal and external factors, the nine types were catalogued, as had not been fully done before, following the example of the sage Wang Zhongjing — the text is to be consulted and referenced accordingly.

This discussion of these conditions is presented in simplified and convenient form, drawing upon the categorizations of Zhang Zhongjing and others, compiled for ease of understanding and practical application.

translation:
Diseases of Fluid Retention: There Are Eight Types
There are also many methods depending on deficiency, excess, cold, and heat conditions, which differ from one another. All the more so in various circumstances.

Retained Fluid (Liu Yin)
When a person with retained fluid is thirsty, has shortness of breath, pain in all four limbs and joints, and a sunken pulse, this indicates retained fluid. When retained fluid is located below the heart, the person feels cold in the back, cold as if a hand were pressed there, or has shortness of breath, vomiting of water, pain in the four limbs and joints, and a deep, thin pulse. For retained fluid, it is appropriate to treat excess fluid accumulation caused by drinking too much flowing water, which leads to hidden fluid retention.

Accumulation Fluid (Pi Yin)
Eastern Water Decoction — for accumulation in the pathways; use Scutellaria and Pinellia Decoction as appropriate; revered lower-body fluid-moving decoction, added to activate the pulse, drawing the fluid energy downward, which becomes sunken over time, causing the person to have gastric vomiting, joint pain, chest and back shortness of breath, and fine pulse.

Phlegm-Fluid (Tan Yin)
A person who was originally robust becomes thin; there are sounds in the intestines — this is called phlegm-fluid. The appropriate treatment is the Ten [Decoctions].

Poria, Cinnamon, Atractylodes, and Licorice Decoction (Fu Gui Shu Gan Tang)
This causes suspended fluid. Atractylodes plain decoction causes thinning; also intestinal daily watery diarrhea; sounds between the intestines; phlegm accumulation fluid; sounds in the gastric diaphragm; fullness in the supporting areas; dizziness — for phlegm-fluid, this decoction is appropriate.

Magical Atractylodes Pill (Shen Shu Jiu)
Treats phlegm-fluid. Remove the skin, dry-roast with ginger, reduce to fine powder one portion. White sesame oil, 5 qian. Water, Cang-zhu (gray atractylodes).

Right side: divide into 2 qian, or 1 qian of Guizhi (cinnamon twig), Baizhu (white atractylodes), take each 1 qian.
Red Poria 2 qian. Poria, Cinnamon, Atractylodes, Licorice Decoction: water, each 1 qian.

This refers to food accumulation and phlegm masses, caused by food and drink failing to digest. [Formula:] Huang Gualou Wan (Yellow Trichosanthes Pill) from Zheng Zhuan (Orthodox Tradition), Modified Two-Aged [Herb] Decoction: Hawthorn fruit 1 qian and a half, cyperus, pinellia, each 1 qian.

Chen [Tang] — for phlegm accumulation. Indicated: Qing Mengshi [Green Mica Stone] 2 liang, calcined, for stubborn drink and food failing to digest. Huang Gualou Wan from Zheng Zhuan, Modified [Two-Aged Herb Decoction].

Qing Mengshi Wan (Green Mica Stone Pill)
Treats damp phlegm internally, removes food accumulation and mucous phlegm. Green mica stone 2 liang, calcined together with saltpeter (niter) 2 liang; wait until the mica stone turns golden in color — that is the measure of completion.

Remove and [combine with] Arisaema (Tiannanxing) 2 liang 8 qian, [processed]. Remove food accumulation and mucous phlegm. White alum, stir-fried 5 qian. Mix with water and dough paste made from [fermented] qu, form into pills the size of wutong seeds. In summer, add qu, mixed with ginger juice and ox bile.

[Continue with processing of] Tiannanxing 2 liang 8 qian, in 4–5 liang [of bile]. Dry in the wind. Transform with saltpeter. Grind to powder, cook together with atractylodes and fermented qu. Fry with ginger. Form paste, mix in ox bile.

[Further instructions on pill-making:] Pills the size of wutong seeds. [Ingredients including] alum dissolved in 5 [units], saltpeter 50 [fen], ground to powder; cook with atractylodes and qu; stir-fry red beans 5 qian; mix with water and fermented qu paste; stir-fry with ginger; [add] Zhishi (bitter orange), Baomian qu paste, mix in ox bile.

Huang Gualou Wan (Yellow Trichosanthes Pill)
Trichosanthes seed and trichosanthes [root], mixed with ginger juice and Banxia (pinellia), pills; hawthorn fruit, shen qu, [formed into] pills the size of [wutong] seeds, processed with ginger.

Bamboo sap [taken] below, 3 [doses]. Treats food accumulation and phlegm masses; indicated when food and drink fail to digest. Huang Gualou Wan from Zheng Zhuan, Modified Two-Aged Herb Decoction: Hawthorn fruit 1 qian and a half, cyperus, pinellia, each 1 qian.

Zheng Zhuan Jia Wei Er Chen Tang (Modified Two-Aged Herb Decoction from Orthodox Tradition)
Treats food accumulation and phlegm masses; disperses food and moves qi.

Alcohol-induced Phlegm Disorders

[Formula ingredients:] Chuanxiong (ligusticum), Suosha (cardamom), Dried ginger sprouts, Baizhu (white atractylodes), Cangzhu (grey atractylodes) — each 8 fen; Chenpi (tangerine peel), Fuling (poria) — each 3 fen; Shenqu (fermented medicated leaven, dry-fried) — each 7 fen. One packet per dose.

[For conditions caused by] drinking and eating [immoderately], not drinking alcohol; when thirst arises, it is appropriate to drink tea water. However, the Ruizhutang Dissolving Phlegm Pills and the Xiangfu Gualou Qingdai Pills may be obtained. The next day vomiting again occurs; [use] Xiangfu Gualou [formula] for vomiting.

Ruizhutang Dissolving Phlegm Pills

Qingdai (indigo naturalis), Damai (barley)... half [portion] to regulate the middle; Banxia (pinellia), dried Manjing [vitex], each one qian; quickly [take] four liang in sequence; take paired with Jinyuan [pills]; for alcohol [conditions use] Xiangfu pills.

Decoct with Tiannanxing (arisaema), flour, white wine; [for] phlegm [use] Zaojia (gleditsia pod), eat one [pill]; each dose, decoct paired portions.

Dry-fry each: For every five to seven liang [of ingredients], right side treats: boil flour, taro, yam, phlegm [accumulation], hawthorn, meat, radish pills, with seeds of Xiangfu (cyperus), Qingtong (indigo copper?), skin inside, apricot kernel, water, raw [ginger].

Xiangfu Gualou Qingdai Pills

Heron-type Phlegm Disorders

When an episode occurs, there is jumping, movement, and pain from the phlegm — unbearable. Many people suffer from this; it is appropriate to use Danxi's [dry-fried formula].

translation:
Miao Ying Dan (Wondrous Response Elixir)

Treats pain and aching throughout the entire body, pulling and hidden pain that is unbearable, migratory pain that moves easily, or suspected lurking wind conditions.

If the mind is restless and sleep is lost, or it is due to phlegm — this is named "control phlegm" and by taking this elixir to control phlegm, the illness will be resolved.

If the pulse is short, the qi is wiry — this indicates cold fluid retention. Or it may be one-sided fluid retention. Or lung fluid retention.

Pulse Method:

The pulse being still weak and faint: if it is sunken, the pulse pattern is one-sided, wiry, raised. Daily fluid accumulation or wiry, slow pulse — fluid accumulation with internal pain. Lung fluid retention: not wiry but only bitter. Or triple knotting, or intermittent — phlegm-fluid pulse is sunken, wiry, slippery, rough, large and small unevenly, obstructing the pathways of fluid and phlegm accumulation.

External Signs of Phlegm-Fluid Retention:

In all diseases presenting with a bright, vivid complexion, after long duration there are retained fluids like the scales of a dried fish — large scales below indicating overflow fluid.

Entering the back with cold fluid: vomiting, in the lung water discharged as thin fluid, water in the chest causing retained fluid, heart distension wanting to drink, water descending daily, large pulse — water is in the kidney, little desire, aversion to qi, water in the body not resolving.

Eyes puffy, the pass above the pulse is sunken and large — this is smoky turbidity surrounding the eyes turning them dark. Use Kongyan Dan. For all hundred diseases — one medicine.

Weight ○○, nine waters, liver and gallbladder below, branch fullness, eyes cold, then ○, smoke surrounding the kidney, heart color below, palpitations, body not resolving.

Eyes not puffy, the pass above the pulse sunken and large — smoky turbidity surrounding eyes turning dark. Use Kongyan Dan. For all hundred diseases — one medicine.

translation:
Diseases of Phlegm-Fluid Retention (Tan-eum)

All phlegm: when water and fluids stagnate over time and become lodged in the body, they afflict the patient. When newly formed, the phlegm is sticky and congealed; it is difficult to expectorate, forms into phlegm that is clear, white, thin, and watery, with little odor or taste.

When there is headache, fever, aversion to cold, and a fishy or mutton-like smell, this is externally contracted surface phlegm. Over time it may be streaked with blood, emerging with a tidal quality, worse at night and doubly severe — this is phlegm from internal damage, arising from the yin aspect.

When there is sour taste, reduction of fire in the flesh, and a purulent, foul color resembling pus, this is phlegm from external invasion affecting the joints; prolonged cases become wind-phlegm, with symptoms around the ears at night, the phlegm being spoken of as "wandering" or "deluded."

Grief and anxiety produce phlegm that lodges in the throat as sour regurgitation, with shortness of breath on exhalation, gurgling sounds, swelling, wind-phlegm, epilepsy, and heat syndrome, or mental confusion and wandering.

Phlegm entering the bones causes the whole body to ache, with groaning, inability to move, and aching pain throughout.

When phlegm obstructs the four limbs it causes convulsions; when it obscures the eyes it causes blackouts; when lodged in the flanks it causes rib-side pain.

Distinguishing the Colors of Phlegm:
Black phlegm indicates heat; yellow phlegm indicates old (chronic) phlegm; white phlegm indicates fire phlegm. These are further categorized as congealed phlegm, and it is also said to involve the flanks.

translation:
Syndrome of Phlegm-Fluid Lodging and Flowing

Common physicians who do not understand the accumulation of various lodging pains habitually use wind-dispelling medicines and medicated plasters, acupuncture and moxibustion — but these are not appropriate for this condition. It should be treated according to the method for phlegm-fluid disorders. When a person suddenly suffers from hidden pain in the back, spine, waist, and legs that is unbearable, moving and shifting without fixed location, connected [throughout the body]...

[The pain is] caused by phlegm in the center. Its manifestation resembles wind-toxin. When phlegm-fluid collects in the heart and abdomen and flows throughout, this condition often causes cold feet, or may transform into swollen pain. At night it may temporarily ease, but then the phlegm returns and the condition continues.

Or [the phlegm] may turn and shift, flowing and lodging, rising and falling, with the fluid coursing upward, only to descend again. Taking the Kongxian Dan (Phlegm-Controlling Pill) — the condition may pass temporarily, and the throat symptom may subside.

When this is mistaken for central phlegm or epilepsy, it is not ordinary. Swallowing large amounts of fluid on an empty stomach leads to this disease: cold [in the interior], or becoming [chronic], and none of these benefit the phlegm.

[The pain] shifts left and right, traveling and attacking the nine regions of the arms, rendering one unable to raise them and observe [their movement].

Formula name: Wondrous Various Pills — dispersing, directing the dispersal of phlegm. The primary [ingredient]: licorice (Gancao).

[Ingredients include:] Gansui, Daj戟, Baijie, Zhusha, dried herbs — fixed amounts, taken with water, divided into nine [pills], until the end, administered in thick liquid.

Gujin, Lujian, Jiangtong, or Hanquan, all of Zhuanshu, plus Chuanshan, added ten [units] for spirit, inserted into the Jing (alarm) [acupoint], Western [region], dried large [dose].

[For] Xinjing (heart fright) with phlegm, blood, or qi, or used by those who, in the twelfth [month], lose their spirit and blood; qi in each [organ] becomes deficient, allowing disease to enter through the center and stomach.

Epidemic Disease Resembling Demonic Possession

[When there is] heart fright, with phlegm, blood, qi deficiency, or when used by those who lose their vitality, allowing the disease to enter through the center and the stomach.

[When the body becomes] agitated and chaotic, rising and falling without peace, and one cannot treat it as demonic [possession] — the patient will certainly die. It is first appropriate to have the patient drink more and listen, for speech, hearing, and vision are [still] functions of the organs.

translation:
Haktingdan (Crane's Crest Elixir)

Melt over heat, remove, apply ginger — three slices, decoct together until reduced by half, add mirabilite (sodium sulfate), mix the juice, apply to the eyes, grind fine. For throat phlegm, grind to powder, take a full dose. Take the above ingredients, grind into powder. Each pill is the size of a cherry. Good formula: alum, calcined, yellow — one pill. Add all ingredients. For stubborn phlegm: realgar — one pill. Cherry-sized. Good formula: white alum, enter all ingredients, for complete resolution of stubborn phlegm and yellow [accumulations]. Grind seeds, large dose, treat with hemp seeds — thirty. Take and form into pills by rolling between the fingers, apply to the area of phlegm. Nine gateway [acupoints] to dissolve, collect and mix pills, pour and mix to irrigate. Voice and sound cannot come out: decoct and dissolve, two portions, center of tower, red jade, five qian, phlegm, alum — or grind into powder, place in a ceramic vessel, decoct in broth to dissolve, with peppermint decoction. Do not further dissolve. Each: thin mint, block the pass — two portions allowed to be vomited up; stand in broth, mix to pour. With little phlegm, it will heal. Do not let flow through the body. Entering phlegm: afterward, the formula uses white [alum], apply seeds to dissolve, apply to the core. Below the liver, the medicine stir-fries two: head, chen [aged], water, decoction, add rhubarb, bamboo sap, linked many times. Hands and feet slightly red, this also becomes pale and consolidated, clearing [the胡] Morning Roc or has chicken wings, turned over by one's own medicine, vomiting downward. Throughout the body there are lumps forming. Cold predominates, forming — this is difficult.

It is appropriate to use the Return-Spirit formula. Can be shifted and moved. Observe and add arisaema and pinellia. Doctor — throughout the body there are lumps forming, cold predominates, forming — this is difficult. Egg-thin juice, not yet decocted, hardened — or phlegm or pain, pain like stone, broken, without [fixed place], or membrane, or blood, or slightly red, also pale and consolidated.

translation:
Dongui Bogam, Internal Medicine Volume 4

Variants: Augmented Xiawei Pill (加味小胃丹), Bamboo Sap Phlegm-Clearing Pill (竹瀝達疾丸)

Phlegm Accumulation (Tan Gyeol)

Phlegm accumulation with coughing: when there is something in the throat that cannot be expectorated, this is phlegm accumulation. In mild cases, use the melon-based formula.

When there is phlegm in the throat, salty [medicines] can dissolve it. Those with mild phlegm accumulation in the throat should use salty and moistening medicines to soften and disperse the hardened nodular phlegm. For mild cases in the throat, use the prescribed formula.

Haefen (sea foam powder), nine sheng of sulfur — for dryness where phlegm cannot be expelled, use this to transform old phlegm. Use Tianmen Dong (Asparagus root) and wine with aconite to warm and transform lung phlegm.

For phlegm that cannot be expelled, use medicines including Banxia (pinellia), to descend qi; Lianqiao (forsythia) for bitterness; to open and harden accumulations; Tianmen Dong to moisten the lung, descend fire, and transform phlegm.

Phlegm Disease Does Not Quickly Lead to Death

When eating is difficult and stools are scanty, with deficiency of qi and stomach excess, qi does not suddenly cause death — those who survive do so because the stomach qi remains. Most cases are due to food accumulation nourishing phlegm-fluid.

Phlegm Conditions Difficult to Treat

When stagnation is substantial with heat, vomiting is difficult; the phlegm-mass cannot be expectorated. When phlegm-heat binds together, it is difficult to treat. Also said: when qi is excessive and phlegm is stubborn, it is difficult to treat. When phlegm is difficult to dissolve and heart qi is affected —

Foamy phlegm with wheezing sounds, panting with labored breathing, coughing with phlegm that constitutes wheezing — this is very difficult to treat. It is best to apply moxibustion early and take phlegm-resolving medicines.

Methods for Expelling Phlegm-Fluid by Emesis

When phlegm is lodged above the diaphragm, one must use emesis to expel it; otherwise it cannot be eliminated. For phlegm lodged in the channels and collaterals, the method of emesis is also required.

Use Erhuang Chen Decoction (Two Yellow and Tangerine Peel Decoction) with ginger juice to induce vomiting, or use bamboo leaf decoction to bring on emesis. When there is qi obstruction and constipation, both purgation and emesis are necessary. One must guard against wind stroke; use Chuanxiong and bitter herbs accordingly.

Methods for Treating Phlegm-Fluid

When the condition arises from fire stirring internally, one must first tonify and then address the phlegm. Use medicinals to smooth the stomach qi and guide out the phlegm. Guide the phlegm downward first, then address the qi. If one attacks prematurely when the patient is deficient, the qi will rebound upward and the condition will worsen.

When fire alone is stirring, use herbs that clear heat and guide out phlegm. First guide the phlegm, then allow the qi to descend smoothly.

In cases where the lung and stomach are affected — arising from retching, drooling, or fluids — if the stomach becomes deficient and the lung also becomes deficient, the condition is difficult to treat. When phlegm accumulates severely with fire, one must still use emesis, as the phlegm in the channels cannot otherwise be removed.

For nighttime leg swelling and deficiency patterns, use Erchen Bami Decoction (Two Aged Ingredients, Eight Flavor Decoction) with bamboo sap and ginger juice.

For phlegm stirred by fire, use the Clear Heat and Guide Phlegm Decoction (see formula in the Phlegm section).

When phlegm is stirred solely by fire, use the Clear Heat and Guide Phlegm Decoction.

For weakness of the spleen with inability to transform and transport, use Liujunzi Decoction (Six Gentlemen Decoction) with bamboo sap and ginger juice.

For cases where deficiency and phlegm combine with cold-dampness, use formulas that dry dampness and guide out phlegm accordingly.

Add bamboo sap and ginger juice as needed.

White Atractylodes (白木), Coptis (青), Second Harmony Pill (二和九), Reed Ginger (蘆薑子), Large [dose] taken orally (大臨下), Fourth Day Drink (飲四日), White Atractylodes powder (白木末).

Regular use: three to five doses of ten pills. Cures qi stagnation, calms the spirit (氣泰), strengthens sinews (筋) and bones (骨). Fritillaria Bulb (Beimu)
Clears phlegm. Another method: wash and dry in sun for three days, grind into powder, mix with paste and frost (a prepared substance), blend together, and take at any time. Peucedanum Root (Qianhu)
Treats cold phlegm. Use three qian, decoct and take. Another formula dissolves phlegm. A pill for phlegm treatment: decoct and take. Can also descend phlegm and expel phlegm accumulation.

Dried Ginger (Ganjiang)
Treats cold phlegm: four qian, decoct and take. Also combined with fresh ginger, one to two qian, regulates the stomach and treats fluid accumulation; decoct and take. Treats phlegm and fluid masses.

Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang)
Eliminates cold phlegm. Used together with Pinellia, it can overpower the stomach; one to two qian, scraped on the right side, decocted with water to treat phlegm; can clear phlegm. Treats phlegm masses; grind to white powder. For phlegm [conditions].

Pinellia (Banxia)
Prepared with ginger according to the method, this is the chief herb. Take nine to ten [pills], add to decoction with coptis, half [portions]; Pinellia combined with Arisaema in oil treats painful phlegm, add half portion to transform large accumulations of phlegm, can clear dampness and phlegm stagnation. Combined with aged tangerine peel, stir-fry, and dissolve phlegm.

Pinellia Qu (Fermented Pinellia)
For those suffering from phlegm who cannot eat, use with bamboo or make into qu (fermented cake) to treat phlegm and accumulated [phlegm]. Also combine with dried pinellia, arisaema, and oil for phlegm, and add [other ingredients]. Prepared with ginger juice according to the standard method; see the full preparation below. Use summer arisaema oil for phlegm.

Also: stir-fry with atractylodes, soak in juice to treat summerheat phlegm, old phlegm, and fire phlegm. Used as an assistant [herb], combined with ginger juice and half [portions] to moisten [the preparation].

translation:
Method for Preparing Pinellia (Banxia/半夏)

Cangzhu (atractylodes) and White Atractylodes are both gathered for therapeutic use. The method for preparing with ginger is described in detail elsewhere in the formulary compendium.

Soak raw Pinellia in water for 3 to 7 days, changing the water 3 to 4 times in succession, then dry in the sun. Use alum and Pinellia together; soak in water, stirring 7 times, place in a basin, and sun-dry overnight. Repeat 3 times with saltpeter and alum, adding cinnamon bark, white cardamom, aucklandia root, pepper, and other medicines — 8 qian, 8 qian, 3 liang respectively — combine with Pinellia and stir together; soak in water, changing 7 to 8 times, then sun-dry by day and expose to dew by night. After 3 repetitions with saltpeter and alum, add green tangerine peel in measured amounts, stir in a vessel daily until the Pinellia is sufficiently prepared; remove, allow to set, and this medicine, when taken, improves the constitution.

Take crushed dried herbs, shepherd's purse, pepper, and other ingredients — grind finely, crush with alum, soak in water, changing 7 to 8 times, sun-dry by day, control drying by night; wash the Pinellia and use with white alum, stirring thoroughly.

Soak 1 to 2 qian; wrap white Pinellia in a packet, leave for 5 days, then sun-dry until thoroughly dry, collect the dried material; place in a vessel and stir daily until sufficient; remove when ready.

Wrap in fish membrane, secure the Pinellia in place for one night, sun-dry during the day, collect and use. This preparation purifies phlegm, reduces fluid accumulation, and clears the digestive system.

Treats phlegm disorders, wind-stroke with impaired movement and loss of speech; research the grinding and administration of phlegm-reducing preparations.

Treats stubborn phlegm that does not respond to standard treatment; grind and administer by decoction.

白芥子
translation:
Water Chestnut (Eleocharis dulcis):
Eliminates phlegm from the bones. Drinking it can expel phlegm from the lung meridian and calm the heart.

Inula flower (Xuanfuhua):
Dissolves phlegm. Applied to the gallbladder region; decocted in water and taken orally, or made into pills to remove phlegm and calm the heart.

Bitter Orange (Zhishi):
Its yin aspect: taken orally for phlegm; Korean use — for gallbladder, water diarrhea; decocted and taken, or made into gelatin pills to calm the heart.

Bitter Orange Peel (Zhike):
Decoct to dissolve phlegm; apply the powder. For the gallbladder, all phlegm and diarrhea can be treated by decoction; taken orally with a belt-like effect; can strengthen the thoroughfare vessel.

Arisaema (Tiannanxing):
Decoct in water for wind conditions; take orally, or roast until golden, add juice, make pills with 7 slices of fresh ginger; effective for relieving lateral phlegm obstruction. Used with chaenomeles and fumigation.

Green Phlogopite (Qingmengshi):
Stops food stagnation and relieves constipation; grind and pound phlegm until sieved out. Make into pills with chaenomeles decoction; process with honey and ginger juice; irrigate with bamboo water. Mixes well.

Chaenomeles (Mugua)

Mume (Wumei):
Used as a main tea for eliminating phlegm; stops hiccups and diaphragm obstruction; the powder can reach phlegm below the diaphragm; decoct and take — all are excellent.

Dongui Bogam, Internal Medicine Section, Volume 2

Melon Stalk (Guadi)
To expel phlegm: use Guadi powder. Stuffing the cardiac region of the stomach causes the person to feel faint, and it can soften stubborn phlegm and dissolve it. See the detailed prescription in the remedies section.

Sea Powder (Haepun / Hai Fen)
When unprocessed, it can treat diseases; entering [the body] it can reduce dampness. Immediately it can dry out and dissolve accumulations. Preparation method detailed in the cardiac section.

Clam Shell Powder (Hapun / Ge Fen)
Burn clam shells into white ash, grind finely, mix with water, form into pills, take orally. Also relieves fire and heat conditions at sea.

Freshwater Clam Shell (Hyeonpae / Xian Ke)
Removes phlegm from the heart and bones; drink the water from boiling them, take with salt water, do not eat.

Acupuncture and Moxibustion Methods
For pathogenic conditions and various abscesses: Juque point, drink medicine, take [the treatment] at Weidao, Zhongfu, Geyu, Weishu, Shenshu, Pishu points. For vomiting and hiccup, connecting the triple burner, not stopping eating.

For conditions where qi is not flowing properly, not responding to treatment, and the patient cannot eat: apply [needling] at Laogong, [treat] obstructions, seal at Weishu, Shenshu points; for the Jing condition, it is appropriate to apply moxibustion early at the stomach region.

At the acupoints, water flows in a manner resembling loose watery stools; when cases are numerous, this is a downward descent of phlegm. The condition appears in a vague and indistinct manner.
